cards.pattern: I recommend we [do X]. Here's why:
cards.quote: I recommend we devote our next sprint to fixing bugs. Here's why:
cards.zh: 我建議我們把下個衝刺全部用來修 bug。理由如下：
cards.why: 結論放第一句，理由編號列在後面。讀者第一秒就知道你要什麼，就算只讀到第一行也能回你 yes / no。
swaps: I'm recommending [X]. Three reasons:
My recommendation: [X]. Here's the reasoning.
cards.pmNote: Minto 金字塔原則：先給答案，再給支撐論點，最後才擺資料。「你從下往上思考，但要從上往下呈現。」
cards.episode: The Minto Pyramid Principle and the SCR Framework

cards.pattern: I'd like to [gavel on this decision] by [time]—the default is that we'll [move forward with X].
cards.quote: I'd like to gavel on this decision at the end of the meeting—the default is that we'll move forward with this approach
cards.zh: 我希望這個決定在會議結束前拍板；沒有異議的話，預設就是照這個方向走。
cards.why: 同時給出「決定期限」和「不回應等於同意」的預設值。把沉默從拖延變成推進，逼對方要嘛拍板、要嘛現在講話。
swaps: Unless I hear otherwise by [Friday], I'll proceed with [X].
Default is [X]—flag it now if you disagree.
I'd like to close this by [date]; silence means we go with [X].
cards.pmNote: 這叫 default-to-action：非同步溝通裡最有效的推進器，也是台灣 PM 寫英文信最少用的一招。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.pattern: We must choose between [X] or [Y]. Should we do X or Y?
cards.quote: We must choose between [X, new request] or [Y, existing item on OSR]. Should we do X or Y?
cards.zh: 我們必須在 X（新需求）和 Y（現有排序中的項目）之間二選一。要做 X 還是 Y？
cards.why: 把開放式討論壓成封閉式選擇題。不留第三條路，對方就沒辦法回你「兩個都做」。
swaps: The choice is between [X] and [Y]—which do you want?
This is an either/or: [X] or [Y].
We can do [X] or [Y] this quarter, not both.
cards.pmNote: Tara Seshan（Stripe / Watershed）觀察：PM 最常見的失敗是暗示「資源很緊」而不是明確給二選一，結果高層永遠回「兩個都做」。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.pattern: I think we should do [option N]. And if we do [N], we're not staffed to do it well. I need [X] to do it right.
cards.quote: I think we should do 3. And if we do 3, we're not staffed to do it well. I need [X] people to do it right.
cards.zh: 我認為我們該選第三案。但如果要做第三案，現在的人力做不好。要做對，我需要 X 個人。
cards.why: 先選定方向、再要資源——順序不能反。先要資源會被讀成討價還價，選完再要就變成「執行這個決定的必要條件」。
swaps: My pick is [N]. If we go with [N], I'll need [X] to execute properly.
Recommend [N]—and [N] requires [X] to do well.
cards.pmNote: 先定優先順序再要 headcount。反過來做會掉進「再給我一個工程師就好」的陷阱。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.quote: Yes, but here's what'll need to change. Should we move forward?
cards.zh: 可以，但有些東西得跟著改。我們要繼續往下走嗎？
cards.why: 表面說 yes、實際把成本攤開，最後把決定權丟回去。對方看到代價多半會自己收回要求——而你一次「不」都沒說過。
swaps: Happy to do it—here's what moves if we do.
We can do this, but [X] will slip. Want me to proceed?
cards.pmNote: Lenny 的五段式說不：前兩段開頭都是 Yes，但實際上都是在說不。
cards.episode: Saying no

cards.pattern: Yes, but not right now because we should stay focused on [X] because of [reasons]. Do you agree?
cards.quote: Yes, but not right now because we should stay focused on X because of XYZ. Do you agree?
cards.zh: 可以，但不是現在——我們應該先專注在 X，因為 XYZ。你同意嗎？
cards.why: 「不是現在」比「不要」好吞。句尾那句 Do you agree? 把它變成需要對方點頭的共同決定，而不是你單方面的拒絕。
swaps: Yes, but I'd queue it for [next cycle]—[reason]. Sound right?
Agreed in principle, wrong timing. OK to revisit in [Q3]?
cards.pmNote: Lenny 說大多數點子都落在這一格：不是壞主意，只是不值得打斷手上的事。
cards.episode: Saying no

cards.pattern: No, but how about we do [Z] instead, which achieves a similar outcome?
cards.quote: No, but how about we do XYZ instead, which achieves a similar outcome?
cards.zh: 不行，但我們改做 XYZ 如何？可以達到差不多的結果。
cards.why: 拒絕之後立刻補一個替代方案。對方真正要的是結果不是那個方案，你把結果給他，就不算真的拒絕他。
swaps: No—but [Z] gets you the same outcome for a fraction of the cost.
I'd push back on the approach, not the goal. What about [Z]?
cards.pmNote: 對同事要像對用戶：聽他的問題，不必照單全收他提的解法。
cards.episode: Saying no

cards.pattern: No, because it's a bad idea for [reasons]. Do you agree?
cards.quote: No, because it's a bad idea for reasons XYZ. Do you agree?
cards.zh: 不行，因為 XYZ 這幾個理由，這是個壞主意。你同意嗎？
cards.why: 敢直接寫 No 再接理由，最後仍留一句確認。台灣人寫英文最常漏掉的就是那句確認——沒有它讀起來像結案，有它才是對話。
swaps: I don't think we should do this, for [reasons]. Where do you land?
My read is this is the wrong call because [X]. Push back if you see it differently.
cards.pmNote: 要說服主管他錯了，Lenny 的建議是先把觀點放一邊，讓事實自己講話。
cards.episode: Saying no

cards.pattern: My recommendation: [X]. [One-sentence reason.]
cards.quote: My recommendation: If you have a choice, use Claude for analysis work. It covers more ground while staying rooted in the actual data.
cards.zh: 我的建議是：如果你有得選，分析工作就用 Claude。它涵蓋的範圍更廣，同時又貼著真實資料走。
cards.why: 把 My recommendation: 當成標籤用，讀者快速掃過去也抓得到。後面一句話講完理由，不拖泥帶水。
swaps: My recommendation: [X].
If I had to pick one: [X], because [reason].
Bottom line: go with [X].
cards.pmNote: 長文件裡把關鍵句加粗標籤，是讓不讀完的人也能拿走結論的最低成本做法。
cards.episode: How to do AI analysis you can actually trust

cards.pattern: I don't think it's worth it for the company; we won't hit our [company-level goals].
cards.quote: I don't think it's worth it for the company; we won't hit our usage and revenue goals
cards.zh: 我認為這對公司來說不划算；我們會達不到使用量和營收目標。
cards.why: 用公司目標而不是團隊目標當理由。高層腦子裡裝的是公司目標，你替他換算好，他就不必自己換算，也更容易站到你這邊。
swaps: This doesn't clear the bar against [company goal].
Measured against [company OKR], this is a net negative.
cards.pmNote: Company first, team second：同一個取捨，用公司目標包裝的說服力遠高於用團隊目標。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.pattern: Both [A] and [B] told us we needed to (1) [action one] and (2) [action two].
cards.quote: Both the results we were seeing in the data and our early traction selling Equals told us we needed to (1) kill free and (2) add friction back to onboarding.
cards.zh: 資料上看到的結果，加上 Equals 早期的銷售成績，兩邊都指向我們必須（1）砍掉免費方案，（2）把 onboarding 的摩擦加回來。
cards.why: 「兩個獨立來源指向同一個結論」比單一數據強得多。再用編號把行動切乾淨，讀者記得走的就是那兩個編號。
swaps: Both [A] and [B] point to the same conclusion: we should [X].
[Data] and [field signal] independently say the same thing.
cards.pmNote: 量化資料 + 銷售現場訊號的交叉驗證，是砍掉一個已上線功能時最站得住腳的證據組合。
cards.episode: Lessons from going freemium: a decision that broke our business

cards.pattern: The real question here isn't [X], or [Y], it's [Z].
cards.quote: The real question here isn't about tech, or specific resources, it's about position.
cards.zh: 這裡真正的問題不是技術，也不是資源多寡，而是站位。
cards.why: 在列選項之前先重新定義問題。你一旦拿到定義問題的權力，後面那份選項清單就是照你的框架長出來的。
swaps: The real question isn't [X], it's [Y].
This isn't a resourcing problem—it's a positioning problem.
We're solving the wrong question. The one that matters is [Y].
cards.pmNote: Shishir Mehrotra 稱之為 eigenquestion：找出那個一旦回答、其他問題就自動有解的問題。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.pattern: We have a tradeoff to make: (1) [option + its precondition], (2) [option + its cost]
cards.quote: We have a tradeoff to make: (1) we can buy them, once we have enough leverage to confront media companies directly, (2) we can take the same strategy, but we have to prepare the rest of Google for the fallout
cards.zh: 我們有個取捨要做：（1）我們可以買下他們，前提是我們有足夠籌碼直接跟媒體公司攤牌；（2）我們可以走一樣的策略，但得先讓 Google 其他部門準備好承受後果。
cards.why: 每個選項後面都掛一個「前提／代價」子句，而不是光列名字。讀者不必自己推演，也看得出你真的把每條路走過一遍。
swaps: We have a tradeoff to make: (1) [X], if [precondition]; (2) [Y], but [cost].
Three paths, each with a price: [A] costs [x], [B] costs [y], [C] costs [z].
cards.pmNote: 選項清單只列名稱等於沒列。每一項都要帶前提或代價，否則高層只會挑聽起來最好聽的那個。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.pattern: It changes the conversation from "Why can't we do this one extra thing?" into "Do you agree that [X] is more important than [Y]?"
cards.quote: It changes the conversation with other teams from “Why can't we do this one extra thing?” into “Do you agree that X is more important than Y?”
cards.zh: 它把跟其他團隊的對話，從「為什麼不能多做這一件事？」變成「你同意 X 比 Y 重要嗎？」
cards.why: 兩句引號對照就講完整個策略。前一句你是守方，後一句對方得表態排序——同一件事換個問法，攻守就易位。
swaps: The question isn't "can we squeeze this in"—it's "what comes out."
Reframing this from "why not" to "instead of what."
cards.pmNote: 公開的專案排序表（OSR）是讓這個改寫成立的前提：沒有清單，就沒有 Y 可以拿來比。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.pattern: The tradeoff is that [downside]. You'll [specific inconvenience], and you'll need to [extra work].
cards.quote: The tradeoff is that it doesn't filter for you. You'll often get validated patterns and half-formed hypotheses presented on equal ground, and you'll need to verify that themes are well-evidenced.
cards.zh: 代價是它不會幫你過濾。你常常會拿到已驗證的模式和半成形的假設被並排放在一起，你得自己確認每個主題證據夠不夠。
cards.why: 推薦完立刻自曝缺點。願意主動講代價的人，讀者反而更信他前面講的優點。
swaps: The tradeoff is that [X].
The cost of this approach is [X].
What you give up: [X].
cards.pmNote: 推薦工具、供應商、技術方案時，主動列出代價會顯著降低對方反覆質詢的次數。
cards.episode: How to do AI analysis you can actually trust

cards.pattern: Best for [use case]. Gives you [less of A] but with [more of B].
cards.quote: Best for highly evidenced themes and now video analysis. Gives you fewer themes but with stronger grounding.
cards.zh: 最適合用在需要強證據支撐的主題，現在也能做影片分析。它給你的主題比較少，但每一個的根據都更紮實。
cards.why: 列選項時每一項都套同一個句型，讀者才能橫向比較。格式一致本身就是說服力——它證明你用同一把尺量過每個選項。
swaps: Best for [use case]. Gives you [less X] but [more Y].
Strongest at [X]; weakest at [Y].
Use when [condition]; avoid when [condition].
cards.pmNote: 供應商評估文件裡，每個選項用同一組欄位描述，比寫得漂亮更重要。
cards.episode: How to do AI analysis you can actually trust

cards.pattern: We knew [short-term cost], with the bet that we'd [long-term gain].
cards.quote: We knew ARR would take a hit short-term, with the bet that we'd drive more companies to get stuck into Equals and drive ARR higher long-term.
cards.zh: 我們知道短期 ARR 會掉，賭的是能讓更多公司深度用上 Equals，長期把 ARR 推得更高。
cards.why: with the bet that 這個接法很好用：它坦承這是賭注不是保證，同時清楚指出賭的是什麼。比 we believe 誠實，也比 we believe 有份量。
swaps: We expect [short-term cost], with the bet that [long-term gain].
Short term this costs us [X]; the bet is [Y].
We're trading [X] now for [Y] later.
cards.pmNote: 寫下「我們賭的是什麼」等於同時寫下了驗收條件——半年後可以直接拿出來對帳。
cards.episode: Lessons from going freemium: a decision that broke our business

cards.pattern: If we decide to take this on now, what happens next quarter? Next year? What ongoing costs do we take on?
cards.quote: If we decide to take this thing on now, what happens next quarter? Next year? What ongoing costs do we take on?
cards.zh: 如果我們現在接下這件事，下一季會怎樣？明年呢？我們會背上哪些持續性的成本？
cards.why: 連續三個問句把時間軸拉長。問句不像斷言那樣顯得在指責，但逼對方自己算一次帳。
swaps: What does this look like in [12 months]?
What ongoing costs are we signing up for?
What's the second-order effect of saying yes here?
cards.pmNote: 業務團隊常以一季為單位思考，產品團隊要把時間軸拉長——這是 PM 在取捨對話裡最容易創造的價值。
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.pattern: We don't want to increase [A] at the expense of [B], or [C] while [D] takes a nosedive.
cards.quote: we don't want to increase speed at the expense of developer experience, or spend more time on new features while quality takes a nosedive
cards.zh: 我們不希望為了提速而犧牲開發者體驗，也不希望把時間都投在新功能、結果品質直線下滑。
cards.why: at the expense of 是書面取捨的標準接法，比 but 精確——它明確指出誰在為誰付出代價。
swaps: ...at the expense of [X]
...without sacrificing [X]
even if it means [X] goes down
cards.pmNote: 指標要成組使用互相牽制，單一指標一定會被優化到扭曲。
cards.episode: Introducing Core 4: The best way to measure and improve your product velocity

cards.pattern: [New approach], a step between [extreme A] and [extreme B].
cards.quote: So this time we decided to require every signup to start a 14-day free trial and input a credit card, a step between a free self-serve product and having to get on the phone with us.
cards.zh: 這次我們決定要求每個註冊都得開 14 天免費試用並輸入信用卡——這是介於「完全免費自助」和「一定要跟我們通電話」之間的一步。
cards.why: a step between A and B 把新方案定位在兩個已知極端之間。讀者不必理解新東西，只要知道它落在哪個位置。
swaps: [X], a step between [A] and [B]
somewhere between [A] and [B]
a middle path: keeps [benefit of A] without [cost of B]
cards.pmNote: 當兩派人各執一端時，把提案描述成「介於兩者之間的一步」比說服任何一方都容易。
cards.episode: Lessons from going freemium: a decision that broke our business

cards.quote: No, this is a bad idea, but we can achieve similar results with a variation of it.
cards.zh: 不行，這是個壞主意，但我們可以用它的變形達到差不多的結果。
cards.why: 把「否決方案」和「保留目標」分開講。你反對的是做法，不是他想要的東西——這一分，對方的防衛心就掉一半。
swaps: The idea's off, but the goal isn't. Here's another route to it.
I'd drop the approach and keep the outcome.
cards.episode: Saying no

cards.pattern: The numbers are unambiguous: [stat one], and [stat two].
cards.quote: The numbers are unambiguous: 55% say AI has exceeded their expectations, and roughly three-quarters of our respondents would say AI has delivered on or surpassed its promise.
cards.zh: 數字很明確：55% 說 AI 超出他們的預期，大約四分之三的受訪者認為 AI 達成或超越了它的承諾。
cards.why: 先下判斷再給數字，而不是給完數字讓讀者自己猜結論。冒號那一下把「數字很明確」變成標題，後面全是佐證。
swaps: The numbers are unambiguous: [data].
The data is clear on this: [data].
One number tells the story: [data].
cards.episode: AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey

cards.pattern: Only [X]% report [downside]. By almost any [domain] standard, these are strong numbers.
cards.quote: Only 17.7% report disappointment. By almost any product standard, these are strong numbers.
cards.zh: 只有 17.7% 表示失望。以幾乎任何產品標準來看，這都是很強的數字。
cards.why: 給完數字要記得替讀者定錨。沒有基準的數字沒有意義，一句 By almost any product standard 就補上了那個基準。
swaps: By any reasonable benchmark, [X].
For context, anything above [Y] is considered strong.
Industry median is [Y]; we're at [X].
cards.pmNote: 台灣人寫英文報告最常漏的一層：數字有了，但沒說「這算好還是壞」。
cards.episode: AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey

cards.pattern: One more pattern worth noting: [finding] ([the number that cuts against you]).
cards.quote: One more pattern worth noting: engineers report the most mixed results on quality later in the survey (51% better but 21% worse, the highest “worse” of any role).
cards.zh: 還有一個值得注意的模式：工程師在後面問到品質時，回答最兩極（51% 說變好、21% 說變差，是所有角色裡「變差」比例最高的）。
cards.why: 主動指出對自己結論不利的資料。願意寫出 but 21% worse 的人，前面那些好數字才會被相信。
swaps: One more pattern worth noting: [X].
It's worth flagging the counter-signal here: [X].
The number that gives me pause: [X].
cards.episode: AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey

cards.pattern: The consistent pattern: [range] on [scope of work].
cards.quote: The consistent pattern: between 3x and 10x time compression on knowledge work that previously required either deep expertise or tedious manual effort.
cards.zh: 一致的模式是：在原本需要深厚專業或繁瑣手工的知識工作上，時間被壓縮 3 到 10 倍。
cards.why: 用區間（3x–10x）而不是單一平均值。區間傳達的是「我看過分佈」，平均值傳達的只是「我算了一下」。
swaps: The consistent pattern: [X].
Across every segment we looked at, [X].
The range is [A] to [B], clustered around [C].
cards.episode: AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey

cards.pattern: This tracks with our earlier finding that [related result].
cards.quote: This tracks with our earlier finding that designers report the lowest quality improvements and the smallest time savings.
cards.zh: 這跟我們前面的發現一致：設計師回報的品質提升最小、省下的時間也最少。
cards.why: This tracks with... 把兩個獨立資料點縫起來，讓讀者覺得你在講一個系統，而不是一堆散落的數字。
swaps: This tracks with [earlier finding].
This is consistent with what we saw in [X].
This lines up with [X] from last quarter.
cards.episode: AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey

cards.pattern: But look farther down the list and a pattern emerges: [X], but [contrast].
cards.quote: But look farther down the list and a pattern emerges: AI is helping PMs produce, but it lags in helping them think.
cards.zh: 但把清單往下看，一個模式就浮現了：AI 幫得上 PM「產出」，卻在幫他們「思考」上落後很多。
cards.why: 先引導讀者的視線（look farther down the list），再給結論。這種寫法讓讀者覺得是自己看出來的，接受度比被告知高很多。
swaps: Look past the top three and a pattern emerges: [X].
The interesting part isn't the top of the list—it's [X].
cards.episode: AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey

cards.pattern: Only [X]% [do it today], but nearly [Y] want it to be.
cards.quote: User research shows the largest demand gap of any task (+27.2pp). Only 4.7% say it's their primary AI use case today, but nearly a third want it to be.
cards.zh: 使用者研究是所有任務裡需求缺口最大的（+27.2 個百分點）。今天只有 4.7% 說這是他們主要的 AI 用途，但將近三分之一希望它是。
cards.why: Only X%... but nearly Y 是把一個數字變成一個機會的標準寫法。落差本身就是論點，不需要你再補一句「所以我們該做」。
swaps: Only [X]% do this today, but [Y]% want to.
Today it's [X]; the demand is [Y]. That gap is the opportunity.
cards.pmNote: demand gap（現況 vs. 想要）是提案裡最有說服力的一種數字，因為它同時證明了問題存在和市場存在。
cards.episode: AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey

cards.pattern: Even the most skeptical group, [X], still shows [result].
cards.quote: 63% of PMs and 83% of founders report that AI saves 4+ hours per week. Even the most skeptical group, designers, still shows 47.5% reporting 4+ hours saved.
cards.zh: 63% 的 PM 和 83% 的創辦人回報 AI 每週省下 4 小時以上。就連最懷疑的一群——設計師——也有 47.5% 回報省下 4 小時以上。
cards.why: 拿對你最不利的子集當證據，反對的人就沒得挑。這是書面論證裡最強的一招，因為它等於幫對方做完了盡職調查。
swaps: Even [the most skeptical group], [result].
Even in the worst-performing segment, [X].
This holds even if you exclude [favorable subset].
cards.episode: AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey

cards.pattern: There are over [absolute number] [things]. This is [X]% above [the low point], and up [Y]% since [recent baseline].
cards.quote: There are over 7,300 open PM roles at tech companies globally, and trending up. This is 75% above the low we saw in early 2023, and already up nearly 20% since the start of this year.
cards.zh: 全球科技公司目前有超過 7,300 個 PM 職缺，而且還在往上。這比 2023 年初的低點高出 75%，光今年開年到現在就漲了近 20%。
cards.why: 絕對值 + 相對低點 + 年初至今，三個角度講同一件事。台灣人寫報告最常只給第一個，讀者就沒辦法判斷這到底算多還是少。
swaps: [N] today—[X]% above [baseline] and up [Y]% since [date].
In absolute terms [N]; relative to [baseline], [X]%.
cards.episode: State of the product job market in early 2026

cards.pattern: This covers [scope]. (It doesn't include [excluded scope].)
cards.quote: Their data looks at roles at tech companies—the most sought-after and lucrative jobs. (It doesn't include roles at non-tech companies and consulting agencies.)
cards.zh: 他們的資料看的是科技公司的職缺——也就是最熱門、待遇最好的那一批。（不包含非科技公司和顧問公司的職缺。）
cards.why: 主動框定資料涵蓋範圍，括號留給排除項。這一句話擋掉了「那 XX 產業呢」這類讓整份報告失焦的追問。
swaps: This covers [X]. (It does not include [Y].)
Scope: [X] only.
Note: [Y] is excluded from this analysis.
cards.episode: State of the product job market in early 2026

cards.pattern: The sample sizes are not huge. [Concrete explanation of how that could distort the result.]
cards.quote: The sample sizes are not huge. Even large companies may not have tons of PMs, and so if a few of these PMs go on to do something great, it can make a company's numbers look great.
cards.zh: 樣本數不算大。即使是大公司，PM 也未必很多，所以只要其中幾個人後來做出成績，就足以讓一家公司的數字看起來很漂亮。
cards.why: 自己先把「這份數據可能怎麼被質疑」寫出來，而且寫得比質疑者更具體。這比等別人問更省事，讀者也會直接把你歸類成可信的人。
swaps: Small n here—[specific way it could mislead].
Treat this as directional; the sample won't support a strong claim.
cards.episode: Which companies accelerate PM careers most

cards.pattern: We can't 100% isolate [the variable]. It could be [A], or it could be [B].
cards.quote: We can't 100% isolate the variable that most contributed to the career trajectory. It could be mentorship that PMs got at the company, or it could be that the company hires strong people.
cards.zh: 我們沒辦法百分之百分離出對職涯軌跡貢獻最大的變數。可能是這些 PM 在公司拿到的指導，也可能只是這家公司本來就招得到強的人。
cards.why: 明說相關不等於因果，並且列出至少兩個替代解釋。寫得出替代解釋，代表你真的想過，而不是拿數字替既有立場背書。
swaps: We can't fully isolate [variable].
It could be [A], or it could be [B].
This is correlation; we haven't established causation.
cards.episode: Which companies accelerate PM careers most

cards.pattern: That said, it doesn't mean that [naive causal reading]. There is still work to do to prove that.
cards.quote: That said, it doesn't mean that new users registering tomorrow and logging more foods will have better retention. There is still work to do to prove that.
cards.zh: 話雖如此，這不代表明天註冊的新用戶只要多記錄飲食就會有更好的留存。要證明這件事還有得做。
cards.why: 給完一個漂亮的相關係數之後立刻踩煞車。這種自我設限反而讓你後續的建議更容易被採納，因為讀者知道你不會誇大。
swaps: This doesn't mean [causal claim]—we'd need [experiment] to say that.
Correlation only. Proving causation needs [X].
cards.pmNote: 相關性分析只能幫你挑實驗題目，不能當實驗結果用。
cards.episode: How to do linear regression and correlation analysis

cards.pattern: Yes, [surface metric improved]. But ultimately [the metric that matters got worse].
cards.quote: Yes, more people made it to the step of using the product. But ultimately fewer of them became engaged, retained users.
cards.zh: 是的，更多人走到了使用產品那一步。但最後真正變成活躍、留下來的用戶反而更少。
cards.why: 先承認對方陣營的數字為真，再把真正重要的指標端出來。你不否認事實，只重新定義什麼算成功——這比爭論數字有效得多。
swaps: Yes, [top-line metric] went up. But [real metric] went down.
The number improved; the outcome didn't.
cards.episode: Lessons from going freemium: a decision that broke our business

cards.pattern: You might be thinking, "[the objection]." That's true, but [why it doesn't change the conclusion].
cards.quote: You might be thinking, “But correlation doesn't imply causation!” That's true, but it's still the best way to identify features with the highest likelihood of driving growth.
cards.zh: 你可能在想：「但相關不等於因果啊！」沒錯，但這仍然是找出最可能帶動成長的功能的最好方法。
cards.why: 把對方腦中的反駁原句寫出來，先承認它對，再說明為什麼不影響結論。讀者的異議一旦被說中，防衛就自動解除。
swaps: You might be thinking, "[objection]." That's true, but [X].
The obvious objection is [X]. Fair—but [Y].
I know: [objection]. Here's why I'd still do it.
cards.episode: How to accelerate growth by focusing on the features you already have

cards.pattern: If you're skeptical that [X], [independent second piece of evidence].
cards.quote: If you're skeptical that this growth is real and likely to be sustained, we're also seeing a surge in demand for tech recruiters.
cards.zh: 如果你懷疑這波成長是不是真的、能不能持續，我們同時也看到科技獵才職缺大幅增加。
cards.why: 直接對懷疑的讀者說話，然後端出一個獨立的第二來源。這比再給一組同源數字有力得多——不同來源指向同一結論才叫佐證。
swaps: If you're skeptical that [X], consider [independent evidence].
If you don't buy [X], here's a second signal: [Y].
cards.pmNote: 領先指標（如獵才職缺）常比主要指標更能說服懷疑者，因為它不受同一組偏誤影響。
cards.episode: State of the product job market in early 2026

cards.pattern: To be clear, I'm not saying [X]. I'm saying [Y].
cards.quote: To be clear, I'm not saying DON'T do freemium. I'm saying it's a scalpel, not a sledgehammer that requires thought.
cards.zh: 講清楚：我不是說「不要做 freemium」。我是說它是手術刀，不是大鎚，需要動腦。
cards.why: I'm not saying X. I'm saying Y. 是防止被曲解最有效的兩句。寫下來的東西會被轉發，你不在場時，這兩句替你辯護。
swaps: To be clear, I'm not saying [X]. I'm saying [Y].
This isn't an argument against [X]—it's an argument for [Y].
Not "never [X]"—"[X] only when [condition]."
cards.episode: Pricing your SaaS product

cards.pattern: Ultimately, [X] didn't work for us. That doesn't mean it couldn't work for you.
cards.quote: Ultimately, freemium didn't work for us. That doesn't mean it couldn't work for you.
cards.zh: 最後 freemium 對我們沒用。這不代表它對你也沒用。
cards.why: 主動把結論的適用範圍縮小。你限縮得越明確，別人就越難用「你的情況跟我不一樣」一句話把你整篇推翻。
swaps: That doesn't mean it couldn't work for you.
Your context may differ—here's what would have to be true for [X] to work.
This is our result, not a universal law.
cards.episode: Lessons from going freemium: a decision that broke our business

cards.pattern: I bet [reader's likely current state]. None of this means you actually need to [the leap they might take].
cards.quote: I bet your team has a half-dozen agent ideas on your backlog right now. None of this means you actually need to build an agent today.
cards.zh: 我猜你們團隊的待辦清單上現在就躺著五六個 agent 的點子。但這些都不代表你今天真的需要做一個 agent。
cards.why: 先把讀者的現況說中，再切斷他可能做出的錯誤推論。None of this means... 專門用來擋「所以你是要我們趕快做囉？」
swaps: None of this means you need to [X] today.
I'm not asking for a decision on [X]—just shared context.
Reading this as "we should build it" would be the wrong takeaway.
cards.episode: Not all AI agents are created equal

cards.pattern: To be fair, [their view] isn't wrong; it's just incomplete.
cards.quote: To be fair, a lot of the time that instinct isn't wrong; it's just incomplete.
cards.zh: 平心而論，那個直覺很多時候並沒有錯，只是不完整。
cards.why: isn't wrong; it's just incomplete 是拆對手論點最漂亮的方式——不否定他，只說他看得不夠遠。對方不必認錯就能改變立場。
swaps: To be fair, [their view] isn't wrong; it's just incomplete.
[X] is true as far as it goes.
That's the right instinct pointed at the wrong layer.
cards.episode: How to debug a team that isn’t working: the Waterline Model

cards.quote: Anything we didn't account for in this document?
cards.zh: 這份文件裡有沒有漏掉什麼？
cards.why: 主動開口要反對意見，而不是等它自己冒出來。你先問，異議就是討論的一部分；別人先提，異議就變成對你的攻擊。
swaps: What did we miss here?
Where does this argument break down?
What would change your mind on this?
cards.episode: How to communicate tradeoffs so leaders will listen

cards.pattern: This is not [the narrow reading], but rather [the correct reading].
cards.quote: This is not a recommendation of singular metrics to track, but rather a basket of metrics that must be used together to be meaningful.
cards.zh: 這不是在推薦單一指標，而是一組必須合在一起看才有意義的指標籃。
cards.why: 預先擋掉最可能的誤用方式。文件會被轉發、被斷章取義，這句話是專門留給那些只讀到一半的人的。
swaps: This is not [X], but rather [Y].
Read this as [Y], not [X].
If you take one thing from this doc, take [Y]—not [X].
cards.episode: Introducing Core 4: The best way to measure and improve your product velocity

cards.pattern: I don't know exactly what's going on here, but it does feel [X]-related.
cards.quote: I don't know exactly what's going on here, but it does feel AI-related.
cards.zh: 我不確定這裡到底發生了什麼事，但感覺跟 AI 有關。
cards.why: 承認不知道，但仍然給方向。這是書面保留的核心：不確定不等於不表態，你可以同時做到「我沒把握」和「我有判斷」。
swaps: I don't know exactly why, but it does look like [X].
I can't fully explain this, but my read is [X].
No clean explanation yet—my instinct says [X].
cards.episode: State of the product job market in early 2026

cards.pattern: [Claim], but a caveat: [X]. [What would invalidate it.]
cards.quote: Gemini sits at a distant 10.6%, but a caveat: this space shifts fast. A few strong model releases or product updates could reshape these rankings quickly.
cards.zh: Gemini 遠遠落在 10.6%，但有個但書：這個領域變化很快。幾個強勢的模型發表或產品更新，就可能迅速改寫這份排名。
cards.why: but a caveat: 用冒號當警示標，後面直接說明「什麼情況下這個結論會失效」。讀者因此知道要盯著什麼看。
swaps: ...but a caveat: [X].
One caveat: this could flip if [Y] happens.
This holds today; [Y] would change it.
cards.episode: AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey

cards.pattern: I don't have the data to prove it, but I suspect [X].
cards.quote: I don't have the data to prove it, but I suspect these end up being the most durable growth inflections.
cards.zh: 我沒有數據可以證明，但我懷疑這些最後會是最持久的成長轉折點。
cards.why: 先自曝證據不足，再給出判斷。順序不能反——先講判斷再補「不過我沒證據」像在打折，先講限制再給判斷反而顯得有膽識。
swaps: I don't have the data to prove it, but I suspect [X].
This is a hunch, not a finding: [X].
Unverified, but my strong prior is [X].
cards.episode: Growth inflections

cards.pattern: This data is from [source], sourced from [method] and thus isn't complete but is directionally correct.
cards.quote: This data is from Crunchbase and Harmonic, which is sourced from public announcements and thus isn't complete but is directionally correct.
cards.zh: 這份資料來自 Crunchbase 和 Harmonic，是從公開發布的消息彙整的，所以不完整，但方向是對的。
cards.why: isn't complete but is directionally correct 是最好用的一組書面保留：一句話同時承認缺陷、又保住結論可用。
swaps: Incomplete, but directionally correct.
Use this for direction, not for precision.
Good enough to decide with; not good enough to quote.
cards.pmNote: 定義資料的用途等級（可拿來決策 vs. 可拿來對外引用）比爭論它準不準有用得多。
cards.episode: Pulling back the curtain on the magic of Y Combinator

cards.pattern: I've worked with [X], though never at [Y] scale, so take this with a grain of salt.
cards.quote: I've worked with 1 and 2-week iterations, though never at a 2-3 person scale, so take this with a grain of salt.
cards.zh: 我做過一週和兩週的迭代，但沒在 2-3 人的規模下做過，所以這段話請斟酌參考。
cards.why: 先講清楚自己的經驗邊界，再叫對方打折。這比乾巴巴的 just my opinion 有用得多——讀者知道該打幾折、在哪裡打折。
swaps: I've done [X], though never at [Y] scale—take this with a grain of salt.
My experience is limited to [X]; adjust for your context.
cards.episode: Ideal sprint length, designer vs. PM roles, running PM team meetings, running post-mortems, best product/executive coaches, and much more

cards.pattern: All that said, I'm not a [domain] expert. Consult [the right owner].
cards.quote: All that said, I'm not a security expert. Consult your local CISO.
cards.zh: 話說回來，我不是資安專家。這部分去問你們的資安長。
cards.why: 兩句話劃清能力邊界並指出誰該負責。不是推卸，是精準交棒——這種寫法反而會讓人更信任你講的其他部分。
swaps: I'm not a [X] expert—loop in [role] before deciding.
This is outside my expertise; [person] should own the call.
Flagging for [team]: this is your call, not mine.
cards.episode: Make product management fun again with AI agents

cards.pattern: I'd like to ask for your help with something. Specifically, I need [type of help] with [specific task/problem]. This is important because [reason].
cards.quote: I'd like to ask for your help with something. Specifically, I need [type of help] with [specific task/problem]. This is important because [reason].
cards.zh: 有件事想請你幫忙。具體來說，我在［某件事］上需要你的［某種協助］。這件事之所以重要，是因為［原因］。
cards.why: 第一句先掛路牌，明說「接下來是一個請求」，對方就不用邊讀邊猜你要什麼。再把「要什麼」和「為什麼」拆成兩句，讓對方能分開評估。
swaps: Quick ask for you:
I need a hand with something—
cards.pmNote: 跨部門要資源時，signpost 讓對方知道這封信需要決定，不是 FYI。
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: I'm asking you because [specific reason]. I'd need this by [date/time]. Is this something you're able to help with?
cards.quote: I'm asking you because [specific reason]. I'd need this by [date/time]. Is this something you're able to help with?
cards.zh: 我來問你，是因為［具體理由］。我需要在［時間］前拿到。這件事你有辦法幫忙嗎？
cards.why: 「為什麼是你」讓請求不像群發信。最後一句給對方一個能光明正大說不的出口（opt-out），反而提高答應率。
swaps: Is this something you have bandwidth for?
Would you be able to take this on?
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: Our current [workload/situation] is unsustainable, and I'm causing [bottleneck] that will impact our ability to hit our targets.
cards.quote: Our current workload is unsustainable, and I'm causing bottlenecks that will impact our ability to hit our targets.
cards.zh: 我們現在的工作量撐不下去，而我正在造成瓶頸，這會影響我們達標的能力。
cards.why: 把「我做不完」翻譯成「公司會受影響」。書面請求要用對方在意的損失包裝，不是用自己的辛苦。
swaps: This is becoming a bottleneck for the whole team.
At the current pace we'll miss [target].
cards.pmNote: 對主管提資源需求時，痛點要落在團隊目標上，不能只落在個人負荷。
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: You do this all the time at [scope], so I'd really like to share my existing [draft/plan] and have you pressure-test it based on your experience.
cards.quote: You do this all the time at the org level, so I'd really like to share my existing prioritization and have you pressure-test it based on your experience.
cards.zh: 你在組織層級天天在做這件事，所以我想把我現有的優先順序給你看，請你用你的經驗幫我壓力測試一下。
cards.why: pressure-test 把一個大請求縮成小請求：對方只要看你已經做好的東西，不必從零思考。同時抬舉了對方的專業。
swaps: I'd love you to poke holes in this.
Could you sanity-check my thinking here?
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: Looking for a brain buddy on this—I have [N] questions. Are you open to answering inline or finding [N] minutes to chat live by [deadline]?
cards.quote: Looking for a brain buddy on this—I have 3 questions. Are you open to answering inline or finding 15 minutes to chat live by the end of this week?
cards.zh: 這件事想找個人一起想——我有三個問題。你想直接在訊息裡回，還是這週內抽十五分鐘聊一下？
cards.why: 先把請求量化（三個問題、十五分鐘），再給「打字回」或「講一下」兩個選項。量化＋二選一，是把「你有空嗎」變成好回答的最快方法。
swaps: I have 2 questions—happy to take them async.
Would inline replies work, or is a quick call easier?
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: I don't want to make an avoidable error in how I'm thinking about [X].
cards.quote: I don't want to make an avoidable error in how I'm thinking about this.
cards.zh: 我不想在這件事的思考上犯一個本來可以避免的錯。
cards.why: 把求助動機說成「避免犯錯」而不是「我不會」，讀起來是謹慎，不是能力不足。書面上這個差別會被存檔。
swaps: I'd rather catch this now than after we ship.
I want to make sure I'm not missing something obvious.
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.quote: I'm glad you want me to own this. I want to say yes, but I don't feel confident I can deliver it and need some support from you.
cards.zh: 很高興你想把這件事交給我。我想答應，但我沒把握能交出成果，需要你這邊的支援。
cards.why: 「我想答應，但」——先接住對方的期待再提條件，保住的信任比直接說「做不到」多得多。
swaps: I want to take this on, and here's what I'd need.
Happy to own it—with one condition.
cards.pmNote: 接下新專案時同步談資源，是 PM 少數能談條件的時機窗口。
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: To do [existing goal] well and also take this on, I'd need us to either deprioritize [X] or staff up [Y] for success.
cards.quote: To do that well and also take this on, I'd need us to either deprioritize the other initiative or staff up the new project for success.
cards.zh: 要把那件事做好、同時又接下這件，我們得二選一：不是把另一個案子降優先，就是幫新案子加人。
cards.why: 不說「不行」，而是把條件寫成兩個具體選項讓對方挑。把決定權交回去，同時逼出一個真正的決定。
swaps: We can do this if we push [X] to next quarter.
Either [X] slips or we add headcount—your call.
cards.episode: On asking for help (even when you really don’t want to)

cards.pattern: This conversation is meant to be an informal chat. I'd like to better understand your world and get your advice as I'm looking to [explain my goals].
cards.quote: This conversation is meant to be an informal chat. I'd like to better understand your world and get your advice as I'm looking to [explain my goals].
cards.zh: 這次就是隨意聊聊。我想多了解你們那邊的狀況、聽聽你的建議，因為我正想做［目標］。
cards.why: 明講「我不是來說服你的」，對方才敢給真情報。書面上尤其需要這句，因為沒有語氣可以傳達善意。
swaps: No agenda here—I'm just trying to understand how you see it.
I'm gathering context, not pitching anything yet.
cards.pmNote: 先蒐集 stakeholder 情報再提案，是 PM 影響力的第一步；情報階段千萬別讓對方覺得在被推銷。
cards.episode: A PM’s guide to influence

cards.pattern: I'm worried that [person X] might bring [argument Y]. Any chance you could chime in during the upcoming meeting or pre-brief [decision maker]?
cards.quote: I'm worried that [person X] might bring [argument Y]. Any chance you could chime in during the upcoming meeting or pre-brief [decision maker Y]?
cards.zh: 我擔心［某人］會提出［某個論點］。你有機會在會議上幫忙說一句，或先跟［決策者］通個氣嗎？
cards.why: 請人幫忙前先講清楚你怕什麼，對方才知道自己要補哪一塊。Any chance you could 是英文裡最不逼人的請求開場之一。
swaps: Would you be up for backing this in the meeting?
Could you give [decision maker] a heads-up beforehand?
cards.pmNote: 會議前先拉盟友（meeting before the meeting），比在會議上臨場辯贏有效得多。
cards.episode: A PM’s guide to influence

cards.pattern: Who are the two best [role]s you know? （取代 "Do you know anyone who..."）
cards.quote: Specifying "two best engineers" reduces the cognitive load put on the recipient and increases the chances that they send you a response.
cards.zh: 指名「兩位最強的工程師」降低了收信者的思考負擔，也提高了他回信的機率。
cards.why: 把開放式問題改成「講兩個就好」，對方的腦力成本從無限變成有限。限量是書面請求能不能拿到回覆的關鍵。
swaps: Who are the top two people you'd point me to?
If you had to name just one, who would it be?
cards.pmNote: 好的請求要 targeted、time-bounded、specific——執行成本壓到一分鐘以內，回覆率才會跳。
cards.episode: How to activate your investor network

cards.pattern: Do you have a minute? （取代 "Sorry to bother you"）
cards.quote: Instead of: "Sorry to bother you." Say: "Do you have a minute?"
cards.zh: 不要寫「抱歉打擾你」，改寫「你有一分鐘嗎？」
cards.why: 台灣人寫英文信最愛開頭道歉。把「抱歉打擾」換成中性提問，請求的份量不變，但你不會先把自己降一階。
swaps: Got a minute?
When you have a moment—
cards.episode: Getting buy-in

cards.pattern: Can you help me understand [X]? （取代 "Sorry, I didn't understand"）
cards.quote: Instead of: "Sorry, I didn't understand." Say: "Can you help me understand?"
cards.zh: 不要寫「抱歉，我沒聽懂」，改寫「可以幫我理解一下嗎？」
cards.why: 同樣一句「我沒懂」，寫成請對方協助就變成合作。書面道歉會被存檔、被轉發，主動語態才不會被讀成能力問題。
swaps: Help me understand the reasoning here.
Can you walk me through that part?
cards.episode: Getting buy-in

cards.pattern: 刪掉 just / actually / quickly："I just wanted to ask..." → "I'm asking..."
cards.quote: "Just" demeans what you have to say. It shrinks your power and influence.
cards.zh: 「just」會貶低你要講的話，它會縮小你的份量與影響力。
cards.why: just、actually、quickly 這三個字是台灣人英文信裡最常見的自我縮小。刪掉之後句子不會變兇，只會變清楚。
swaps: I have a question. (不是 I have a quick question.)
I'd like to propose... (不是 I just think...)
cards.episode: Getting buy-in

cards.pattern: Thank you for our conversation about [specific challenge they mentioned]. I've been thinking about your approach to [topic], and I wanted to share an insight from my experience with [relevant situation].
cards.quote: Thank you for our conversation about [specific challenge they mentioned]. I've been thinking about your approach to [topic], and I wanted to share an insight from my experience with [relevant situation].
cards.zh: 謝謝你上次談到［某個挑戰］。我一直在想你對［主題］的做法，想分享一個我在［類似情境］的心得。
cards.why: 追進度的信不要只寫「想跟進一下」。先還一點價值再開口，對方回信的動機就從人情變成划算。
swaps: Following up with something that might be useful:
One thought since we last spoke:
cards.pmNote: 面試後的 follow-up 附一個具體洞見（甚至小 prototype），比制式感謝信有效得多。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.pattern: I'll keep you informed as I [continue the process]. Are you open to [specific action] on [day and time]?
cards.quote: I'll keep you informed as I speak with others on the team. Are you open to debriefing next Thursday after 2 p.m. PT?
cards.zh: 我跟團隊其他人談的進度也會同步給你。下週四下午兩點後方便一起回顧一下嗎？
cards.why: 收尾不寫「有空再回」，而是給一個指定時段，對方只要回 yes/no。同時暗示你這邊有進度在跑，不是在原地等。
swaps: Would Thursday after 2 work, or should I propose another slot?
I'll assume next Tuesday unless you say otherwise.
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.pattern: Ping me again in [a month / three months] and let's revisit.
cards.quote: If you're open to the idea but aren't sure, tell the person to ping you again in a month (or three months) to revisit the idea.
cards.zh: 如果你對這件事有興趣但還不確定，就請對方一個月（或三個月）後再來提醒你一次。
cards.why: 把「再說」寫成一個有日期的動作：既不用當下拒絕，也把追蹤責任交還給對方。這是英文職場最常見的溫和推遲。
swaps: Circle back with me in Q3 and we'll look again.
Not now, but ask me again after launch.
cards.pmNote: Lenny 說一半以上的人根本不會再來問——這個推遲等於免費的過濾器。
cards.episode: On saying no

cards.pattern: I'll check back in [a week] or so—no need to answer right now.
cards.quote: In such cases, offer to check back in a week or so, giving them time to think about it.
cards.zh: 遇到這種狀況，就主動說一週後再來問一次，給對方時間想。
cards.why: 主動宣告「我一週後再問一次」，把追蹤變成事先講好的約定。第二次追就不會顯得是在催人。
swaps: No rush—I'll follow up next week.
Take your time; I'll ping you Friday.
cards.episode: The Magic Loop

cards.pattern: After [the intro/help lands], send a note back to the person who connected you and tell them what came of it.
cards.quote: You should send a thank-you note to the person who made the connection to close the loop and let them know that their effort did not go to waste.
cards.zh: 你應該回一封感謝信給幫你牽線的人，把這個迴圈收起來，讓他知道他的力氣沒有白費。
cards.why: 追進度不只追人家欠你的，也包含回報結果。close the loop 是下次還請得動同一個人的原因，而幾乎沒有人做。
swaps: Closing the loop on the intro you made:
Wanted you to know how that turned out—
cards.pmNote: Sam 三年寄了 2,626 個請求給投資人，1,664 個有回覆——高回覆率來自每次都收尾。
cards.episode: How to activate your investor network

cards.pattern: I truly wish I had the time. Unfortunately, I've got too much on my plate right now and need to prioritize other things. Can I [smaller alternative] instead?
cards.quote: I truly wish I had the time. Unfortunately, I've got too much on my plate right now and need to prioritize other things. Can I answer your questions over email?
cards.zh: 我真的很希望自己有時間。可惜我現在手上事情太多，必須先顧好別的。要不要改成我用 email 回答你的問題？
cards.why: 拒絕三段式：先表遺憾、再給一個不可辯論的理由（我的優先順序）、最後補一個更小的替代方案。對方拿到東西就不會覺得被打槍。
swaps: I wish I could. Right now I need to protect [priority].
Can't do a call, but happy to help async.
cards.episode: On saying no

cards.pattern: Happy to help! Can we keep this to email to start? I'm trying to cut back on [calls], and I can often be even more helpful over email.
cards.quote: Happy to help! Can we keep this to email to start? I'm trying to cut back on calls, and I can often be even more helpful over email.
cards.zh: 很樂意幫忙！可以先用 email 談嗎？我正在減少通話，而且用寫的我通常還能幫上更多忙。
cards.why: 這不是拒絕，是降規格：把「開會」降成「寫信」。理由還講成對方能得到更好的服務，等於拒絕了形式卻沒拒絕人。
swaps: Can we start async and see if a call is still needed?
Happy to help—email works better for me.
cards.episode: On saying no

cards.pattern: I have a blanket rule of no [category], which I have in place in order to protect [what matters]. I hope you understand.
cards.quote: I have a blanket rule of no talks, events, or podcasts, which I have in place in order to protect my writing/creative time. I hope you understand.
cards.zh: 我有一條一律不接演講、活動、podcast 的規則，設這條規則是為了保護我的寫作時間。希望你能理解。
cards.why: 講「規則」而不是「這次不行」，對方就無法討價還價，也不會覺得是針對他。再補上規則保護的東西，聽起來像原則不像藉口。
swaps: I have a policy of not taking on new projects until [date].
I don't say yes to anything on the spot—that's a rule for me.
cards.episode: On saying no

cards.quote: "My heart says yes, but my schedule says no."
cards.zh: 我的心說好，但我的行事曆說不行。
cards.why: 把拒絕的責任推給行事曆而不是意願，對方不會覺得是自己不夠格。短到可以直接貼進 Slack。
swaps: I want to, but the calendar says otherwise.
Willing but not able right now.
cards.episode: On saying no

cards.pattern: I'm still totally on board, but I wanted to just check—how important and timely is [X] to your team? If it's not that big of a deal, I'd love to skip it or push it out.
cards.quote: I'm still totally on board with giving it, but I wanted to just check—how important, and timely, is this presentation to your team? If it's not that big of a deal, I'd love to skip it, or push it out.
cards.zh: 我還是完全願意講，只是想確認一下——這場簡報對你們團隊有多重要、多急？如果沒那麼要緊，我會很想跳過或延後。
cards.why: 已經答應的事想反悔，先聲明「我沒有要落跑」，再把決定權交給對方。多數時候對方會直接放你走。
swaps: Still happy to do it—just checking how load-bearing it is.
Is this a must-have, or a nice-to-have right now?
cards.episode: Part 2: Time management techniques that actually work

cards.pattern: I noticed [our meeting] is coming up. Any chance we could skip it and knock it out over email async?
cards.quote: Hey Michelle, I noticed our meeting is coming up later this week. Any chance we could skip the meeting and knock it out over email async?
cards.zh: Michelle 你好，我看到我們這週稍晚有個會。有機會跳過會議、直接用 email 非同步處理掉嗎？
cards.why: 不是取消而是換形式。Any chance we could 讓對方拒絕起來毫無成本，所以反而容易點頭。
swaps: Could we handle this over email instead?
Any chance we turn this meeting into a doc?
cards.episode: Part 2: Time management techniques that actually work

cards.pattern: Bad news. I won't be able to make [X]. Something timely came up, and I need to prioritize it.
cards.quote: Hey Steven, bad news. I won't be able to make the coffee chat we have coming up next week. Something timely came up, and I need to prioritize it.
cards.zh: Steven 你好，壞消息。下週約好的咖啡我沒辦法去了。臨時有件很趕的事，我得先處理它。
cards.why: 壞消息放最前面、不鋪陳、不過度道歉。理由給一句就好，寫太多反而像在求原諒。
swaps: Bad news—I need to cancel [X].
Sorry for the late notice: I can't make it.
cards.episode: Part 2: Time management techniques that actually work

cards.quote: Can you tell me the salary band for this level? Happy to let you know if it's within my range, and we can discuss specific numbers later when I've met the team.
cards.zh: 可以告訴我這個職級的薪資帶嗎？我很樂意回覆你在不在我的範圍內，具體數字等我見過團隊之後再談。
cards.why: 被問期望薪資時反問級距，還附上一個「之後再談」的時間點——不回答但不失禮，是整場談判最關鍵的一句話。
swaps: What range is budgeted for this role?
I'd rather understand the band first before naming a number.
cards.pmNote: 談判從第一通 recruiter 電話就開始了；先報數字的人幾乎一定吃虧。
cards.episode: The 10 commandments of salary negotiation

cards.pattern: 收到 "give me your number and I'll make it happen" 時，不要回數字。
cards.quote: What recruiters say: "If you give me your number, I will make it happen for you." What they mean: "I'll get you something lower, but kinda close to what you asked for."
cards.zh: recruiter 會說：「你給我一個數字，我幫你搞定。」他真正的意思是：「我會給你一個低一點、但跟你要的差不多的數字。」
cards.why: 這句話幾乎每個 recruiter 都會寫。認得出來，你就不會把自己的底價先打進 email 裡。
swaps: I'd rather see the offer first.
Let's start from what the role is budgeted at.
cards.pmNote: 大公司薪資多由 compensation committee 決定，recruiter 未必有加碼權限。
cards.episode: The 10 commandments of salary negotiation

cards.pattern: I've received new information since we last spoke—[another offer / a counteroffer from my current team].
cards.quote: Most companies will consider "new information," like another offer, to reopen a negotiation. Don't forget, an offer to stay from your existing company also counts!
cards.zh: 多數公司會因為「新資訊」（例如另一個 offer）而重啟談判。別忘了，現職公司的留任提案也算數。
cards.why: 書面談薪要有「新資訊」才有正當理由重開談判。現職留任 offer 也算籌碼，是台灣人最常忽略的一張牌。
swaps: Something has changed on my end since we last spoke.
I've got a new data point I should share with you.
cards.episode: The 10 commandments of salary negotiation

cards.quote: I'm genuinely excited about this opportunity and can see myself making an impact. I'd love to discuss a few details to make sure we're aligned on expectations.
cards.zh: 我對這個機會真的很興奮，也能想像自己做出貢獻。我想討論幾個細節，確保我們對期待的認知一致。
cards.why: 談條件的標準開場：先把「我要來」講死，再說「有幾個細節」。熱情在前、議價在後，對方才不會以為你在猶豫。
swaps: I'm in—there are just a couple of things I'd like to align on.
Excited about this. A few details before we finalize:
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.pattern: What's the chance that we could explore a slightly different structure for [the compensation package]?
cards.quote: What's the chance that we could explore a slightly different structure for the compensation package?
cards.zh: 我們有多少機會可以試試看稍微不一樣的薪酬結構？
cards.why: 用機率問句代替要求。what's the chance 給了對方說「不高」的空間，反而讓他願意去幫你問。
swaps: Is there any flexibility on how this is structured?
How much room is there to reshape this?
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.quote: I appreciate the strong offer. I'm wondering if we could find a way to bridge the gap between this and what would make it a complete win for both of us.
cards.zh: 謝謝你們給了很好的條件。我在想，我們能不能想辦法把這個數字和「雙方都完全滿意」之間的落差補起來。
cards.why: 先肯定 offer 再談落差，並用 for both of us 把加薪講成雙贏。書面談判最忌讓對方覺得你站在對立面，因為信會被轉發。
swaps: Can we close the gap between this and [number]?
What would it take to get us both to yes?
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.quote: I'm thinking about how I can deliver the most value in this role. Would it make sense to discuss how the compensation structure could align with those key objectives?
cards.zh: 我一直在想我在這個職位上能交出最大的價值。要不要討論一下薪酬結構怎麼跟這些關鍵目標對齊？
cards.why: 把薪資綁在「我要交付什麼」上，談錢就變成談績效設計。這在書面往返裡特別有用，因為這封信會被轉給更多人看。
swaps: Could we tie part of this to the outcomes we just discussed?
I'd like comp to reflect the scope we've been talking about.
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.quote: This looks promising, and I'm eager to move forward. Could we set up a quick call to discuss a few adjustments that might work better for everyone involved?
cards.zh: 這看起來很有希望，我也很想往下走。我們可以約個短會，聊幾個對大家都更合適的調整嗎？
cards.why: 「有進展＋想推進」再接「幾個調整」，保住動能的同時開了門。書面談判最怕沉默，這句把球丟回去但沒讓流程停下來。
swaps: Promising—can we grab 15 minutes to fine-tune a couple of things?
I'd like to move forward; a few adjustments first.
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.quote: I want to be transparent—I have a few opportunities I'm considering right now. I'm most excited about our discussions and want to ensure we find the right fit for both.
cards.zh: 我想坦白說——我手上還有幾個機會在考慮。我最期待的是我們這邊的討論，也想確保這對雙方都是對的選擇。
cards.why: 講有別的機會但不威脅，還說最想來這裡。壓力來自事實而不是語氣——這是不撕破臉的施壓寫法。
swaps: Being upfront: I'm in conversations elsewhere too.
I'd rather be transparent about my timeline than play games.
cards.pmNote: Niya 說你不需要真的拿到多個 offer——能說「我正在跟其他公司談」就夠了。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.pattern: I'm making a significant career decision and want to be thoughtful. I have a few conversations in progress. I expect to be ready to make a decision by [specific date].
cards.quote: I'm making a significant career decision and want to be thoughtful. I have a few conversations in progress, but I'm particularly excited about this opportunity. I expect to be ready to make a decision by [specific date].
cards.zh: 這是一個重大的職涯決定，我想想清楚。我手上還有幾個對話在進行，但我對這個機會特別有興趣。我預計在［日期］前能做決定。
cards.why: 自己訂決策日期，就不會被對方的限時 offer 綁架。主動給日期比拖延更顯得專業。
swaps: I'll have an answer for you by [date].
Does that timeline work with your hiring process?
cards.pmNote: Jacob 說收到 offer 後不到三到五個工作天就答應，通常代表你動作太快了。
cards.episode: The ultimate guide to negotiating your comp

cards.pattern: 冷請求三原則：targeted（只寄給真的相關的人）／time-bounded（一分鐘內可完成）／specific（範圍寫死）。
cards.quote: Targeted: Only send them to the people who are relevant. Time-bounded: Ideally, executing the request should take less than a minute.
cards.zh: 精準：只寄給真的相關的人。有時限：理想上，執行這個請求應該花不到一分鐘。
cards.why: 陌生請求的回覆率不是靠文筆，是靠「執行成本」。把可完成時間壓到一分鐘以內，回覆率才會跳。
swaps: This should take you under a minute:
One reply-all-length answer is all I need.
cards.pmNote: 投資人不回信通常不是因為你用光了人情，而是因為你的請求寫得太難執行。
cards.episode: How to activate your investor network

cards.pattern: In general, people like being helpful. By not asking for things, you're denying other people that joy.
cards.quote: In general, people like being helpful—especially investors! By not asking for things, you're denying other people that joy.
cards.zh: 一般來說，人是喜歡幫忙的——投資人尤其如此！你不開口，等於剝奪了別人得到那份快樂的機會。
cards.why: 重寫冷開場心態的一句話。不寄信不是客氣，是把對方幫忙的機會也拿走了——這個角度能直接降低開口的心理成本。
swaps: I'd rather ask than assume you're too busy.
Saying no is completely fine—I'd still rather ask.
cards.pmNote: 「人情籌碼有限」是錯覺；請求品質才是限制條件。
cards.episode: How to activate your investor network

cards.pattern: In this post, I'll walk through [X] and show you how to use it as [用途] when [情境].
cards.quote: In this post, I'll walk through the model and show you how to use it as a practical diagnostic tool when a team is underperforming.
cards.zh: 這篇文章我會把這個模型走一遍，並示範團隊表現不佳時該怎麼把它當成實用的診斷工具。
cards.why: 先講「我會做什麼」再講「你能拿它幹嘛」，讀者兩秒內就知道要不要往下讀。關鍵在 as a practical diagnostic tool when...——它把抽象內容綁到一個具體使用時機上，讀者會自動對號入座。
swaps: In this doc, I'll lay out [X] and how to apply it when [情境].
This memo walks through [X] and how we'd use it in [情境].
cards.pmNote: 文件開場的職責不是介紹，是幫讀者做「要不要花時間」的決策。
cards.episode: How to debug a team that isn’t working: the Waterline Model

cards.pattern: By the end, you should be better equipped to [能力1], [能力2], and [能力3] instead of [常見的錯誤做法].
cards.quote: By the end, you should be better equipped to slow down in those "something's off" moments, identify the real source of friction on a team, and fix the right problem instead of defaulting to people changes.
cards.zh: 讀完之後，你應該更有能力在那些「哪裡怪怪的」時刻慢下來、找出團隊摩擦的真正來源，並修對問題，而不是動不動就換人。
cards.why: 把交付成果寫成讀者的「新能力」而不是文件的「章節清單」，讀者買的是變化不是目錄。最後那個 instead of [錯誤做法] 尤其厲害——同時告訴你會得到什麼、會停止做什麼蠢事。
swaps: By the end of this doc, you'll be able to [X] without [錯誤做法].
After reading, you should be able to [X] rather than [預設做法].
cards.episode: How to debug a team that isn’t working: the Waterline Model

cards.pattern: By the time you finish reading this [文件], you'll understand [A], [B], and [C]—with [附加物] and [附加物].
cards.quote: By the time you finish reading this post, you'll understand the three types of agents, how to decide which initiatives to prioritize, and how to avoid common pitfalls—with specific recommended tools and platforms and tons of real-life examples.
cards.zh: 讀完這篇，你會搞懂三種 agent 的類型、怎麼決定先做哪個專案，以及怎麼避開常見的坑——還附上具體工具平台推薦和大量真實案例。
cards.why: 三項承諾用平行結構排開（一個名詞組＋兩個 how to），節奏一致所以掃過去毫不費力。破折號後面加「附贈品」是把讀者往下推的最後一腳。
swaps: By the end of this doc you'll know [A], [B], and [C].
This doc covers [A], [B], and [C]—plus [附加物].
cards.episode: Not all AI agents are created equal

cards.pattern: In this [文件], I'll show you how to [目標]. You'll learn about [N] [問題類型] that silently break [你在乎的東西].
cards.quote: In this post, I'll show you how to get relevant and verified insights you can trust. You'll learn about four failure modes that silently break your AI-supported insights.
cards.zh: 這篇我會示範怎麼拿到你信得過、經過驗證的洞察。你會學到四種會悄悄毀掉 AI 分析結果的失敗模式。
cards.why: silently break 這個動詞組是重點：它暗示「你現在正在踩雷但不知道」，製造出讀者非讀不可的缺口。純寫 four common mistakes 就沒有這股拉力。
swaps: You'll learn the [N] [問題] that quietly derail [X].
I'll walk through [N] [問題] most teams miss.
cards.episode: How to do AI analysis you can actually trust

cards.pattern: Below, I'll unpack each of these steps, but to give you a glimpse of where we'll end up, here are [具體產出].
cards.quote: Below, I'll unpack each of these steps, but to give you a glimpse of where we'll end up, here are five lines you can use to effectively say no.
cards.zh: 下面我會一步一步拆解，但先讓你瞄一眼最後會走到哪裡：這裡有五句可以直接拿去用的婉拒說法。
cards.why: a glimpse of where we'll end up 是把結論預告在前面卻不破壞後面的閱讀動機——讀者知道有東西可拿，才願意陪你走完推導。這是長文件最常缺的那一句。
swaps: I'll go through each step below, but here's the punchline up front: [結論].
Details below—but to save you the scroll, here's [產出].
cards.pmNote: 長文件在開場給一個「可帶走的東西」，被讀完的機率會高很多。
cards.episode: Saying no

cards.pattern: Below, you'll find what I believe is the most [形容詞1], [形容詞2], and [形容詞3] [產出] for [用途].
cards.quote: Below, you'll find what I believe is the most actionable, specific, and straightforward framework for crafting a strategy, for both your product and your company.
cards.zh: 下面是我認為最能落地、最具體、也最直白的策略制定框架，產品層級和公司層級都適用。
cards.why: what I believe is 這五個字讓極強的主張變成可接受的個人判斷，不會顯得自吹。三個形容詞排比又把「好在哪」講死，讀者不必自己猜。
swaps: Below is what I think is the clearest [產出] for [用途].
What follows is, in my view, the most practical way to [X].
cards.episode: Strategy Blocks: An operator’s guide to product strategy

cards.quote: You think from the bottom up, but you present from the top-down.
cards.zh: 思考是由下往上，報告卻要由上往下。
cards.why: 一句話講完整個金字塔原則，而且是用對比句型（bottom up / top-down）把兩件事釘在一起，好記到可以直接在 review 會議上引用。台灣人寫文件最常犯的就是照著自己的推導順序寫。
swaps: Lead with the conclusion, not the journey.
Give away the punchline.
cards.pmNote: Minto 金字塔：先講結論 → 幾個支撐論點 → 每個論點配數據。
cards.episode: The Minto Pyramid Principle and the SCR Framework

cards.pattern: Below, I'll share a [N]-step process for [目標], with real-life examples from [樣本].
cards.quote: Below, I'll share a three-step process for finding your activation metric, with real-life examples from a dozen companies.
cards.zh: 下面我會分享一套三步驟流程，教你找出自己的啟用指標，並附上十幾家公司的真實案例。
cards.why: 數字（three-step、a dozen）讓承諾變得可以驗收，讀者知道篇幅大概多長、證據有多厚。沒有數字的 I'll share some thoughts 讀起來就像還沒想清楚。
swaps: Below is a [N]-step approach to [X], with examples from [樣本].
I'll lay out [N] steps, each with a worked example.
cards.episode: How to determine your activation metric

cards.pattern: In this [文件], I'll walk you through [產出1]; [產出2]; and [產出3].
cards.quote: In this post, I'll walk you through three ways to create component libraries that consistently create great mocks; team workflows to reduce rework; and a step-by-step guide on how prototypes should be used.
cards.zh: 這篇我會帶你走過三件事：怎麼建出能穩定產出好 mock 的元件庫；怎麼設計團隊流程來減少重工；以及一份原型該怎麼用的逐步指南。
cards.why: 三個產出各自帶子句，所以改用分號而不是逗號分隔——這是英文文件裡處理「長項目清單」的正規做法，用逗號會糊成一團。
swaps: This doc covers [A]; [B]; and [C].
Three parts below: [A], [B], and [C].
cards.episode: How to get your entire team prototyping with AI

cards.pattern: Though many factors contribute to [壞結果], nothing is more certain to cause [壞結果] than [根本原因].
cards.quote: Though many factors contribute to a project's failure, nothing is more certain to cause a project to fail than a misunderstanding of the problem you are solving.
cards.zh: 專案失敗的原因很多，但最必然導致失敗的，是搞錯了你在解的問題。
cards.why: 先讓步（Though many factors...）再收斂到單一主因，讀起來像審慎判斷而不是誇大。台灣人寫英文常直接下 The main reason is...，少了這個讓步步驟就顯得武斷。
swaps: While [X], [Y], and [Z] all matter, nothing predicts [結果] more than [主因].
Many things went wrong here, but the one that mattered was [主因].
cards.episode: A Three-Step Framework For Solving Problems 👌

cards.pattern: We recognized too late that the real problem we should have been solving was not [表面問題], but instead [真問題].
cards.quote: We recognized too late that the real problem we should have been solving was not "travelers want to hang out with other travelers", but instead, "travelers want to find high quality non-touristy things to do."
cards.zh: 我們太晚才發現，真正該解的問題不是「旅客想跟其他旅客一起玩」，而是「旅客想找到高品質、不觀光客的行程」。
cards.why: not [X] but instead [Y] 是修正問題定義最乾淨的句型，而且把兩個問題都用引號寫成使用者的話，對照一目了然。承認 too late 反而增加可信度。
swaps: The problem isn't [X]—it's [Y].
What we were actually solving for turned out to be [Y], not [X].
cards.pmNote: 問題陳述寫錯，後面所有設計與工程投入都會偏。
cards.episode: A Three-Step Framework For Solving Problems 👌

cards.pattern: The more you need to explain it, the less clear [X] ends up being.
cards.quote: The more you need to explain it, the less clear the problem ends up being.
cards.zh: 你越需要解釋它，代表這個問題其實越不清楚。
cards.why: the more... the less... 這個對稱結構讓一句判準句變得像格言，好記好轉貼。用在自檢或給同事回饋都成立。
swaps: If it takes a paragraph to explain, it isn't one problem.
Length here is a signal we haven't narrowed it down yet.
cards.pmNote: 好的問題陳述應該一句話寫得完。
cards.episode: A Three-Step Framework For Solving Problems 👌

cards.quote: It's agnostic of a solution. Resist the urge to jump to a solution this early.
cards.zh: 它要與解法無關。忍住現在就跳到解法的衝動。
cards.why: agnostic of a solution 是矽谷文件裡的固定說法，比 without mentioning a solution 專業得多。Resist the urge to 則是給讀者台階，把要求寫成同理而不是命令。
swaps: Keep this section solution-agnostic.
We'll get to approaches below—this section is only about the problem.
cards.episode: A Three-Step Framework For Solving Problems 👌

cards.pattern: [使用者族群] are [做出某行為] too often because [原因].
cards.quote: Lyft drivers are cancelling rides too often because the passengers are too far away.
cards.zh: Lyft 司機取消訂單的次數太高，因為乘客距離太遠。
cards.why: 主詞是人不是系統、動詞是可觀察的行為、because 後面掛一個可驗證的假設——一句話同時給了現象和待驗證的因果。整句沒有任何解法暗示。
swaps: [族群] keep [行為] because [假設原因].
[族群] are [行為] at [數字], driven by [假設原因].
cards.pmNote: 問題陳述裡的 because 是假設，不是結論——後面要拿證據補。
cards.episode: A Three-Step Framework For Solving Problems 👌

cards.pattern: The problem isn't that [表面診斷]; it's that [真正診斷].
cards.quote: The problem isn't that they lack ideas; it's that they try to prioritize fundamentally different kinds of systems as if they were the same thing.
cards.zh: 問題不在於他們沒有點子，而在於他們把本質上不同的系統當成同一種東西來排優先順序。
cards.why: 先否定讀者腦中最現成的解釋，再塞進真正的診斷——這個順序會讓讀者覺得「你比我想得深」而不是「你在教我」。分號比句號更能把兩半綁成同一個判斷。
swaps: It's not that [X]; it's that [Y].
The issue isn't [X]. It's [Y].
cards.episode: Not all AI agents are created equal

cards.pattern: Before you can decide [大決定], you need to answer a more basic question: [更基本的問題]?
cards.quote: Before you can decide which agent to build first, you need to answer a more basic question: What type of agent is each idea actually proposing?
cards.zh: 在決定先做哪個 agent 之前，你得先回答一個更基本的問題：每個點子提出的到底是哪一種 agent？
cards.why: 把讀者原本急著回答的問題往後推一格，等於重新設定整份文件的議程，而且不需要否定任何人。冒號後面直接甩出那個問題，讀者會不自覺開始在腦中回答。
swaps: Before we pick [方案], we need to agree on [前提].
The prior question is [X].
cards.episode: Not all AI agents are created equal

cards.pattern: [歸咎人] for problems that are actually [結構性的] is one of the biggest [領域] traps there is.
cards.quote: Blaming people for problems that are actually structural is one of the biggest leadership traps there is.
cards.zh: 把其實是結構性的問題怪到人頭上，是領導者最大的陷阱之一。
cards.why: one of the biggest ... traps there is 是英文裡把主張講重但不封死的固定說法（沒說「最大」，但氣勢等同）。用 trap 而不是 mistake，暗示這是誰都會踩的坑，讀者比較不會對號入座。
swaps: Treating [結構問題] as a people problem is one of the easiest traps to fall into.
It's tempting to read this as [人的問題]—I think it's [結構問題].
cards.episode: How to debug a team that isn’t working: the Waterline Model

cards.pattern: [X] (or so you think), [Y] (or so they say), yet [症狀1], [症狀2], and [症狀3].
cards.quote: You've set a clear goal (or so you think), your team's bought in (or so they say), yet timelines keep slipping, execution is messy, and you're having the same conversations over and over.
cards.zh: 你訂了明確的目標（你以為），團隊也買單了（他們嘴上說），可是時程一直延、執行一團亂，而且同樣的對話講了一遍又一遍。
cards.why: 括號裡的 (or so you think) 是書面英文特有的低成本吐槽——沒有語氣可用時，用括號製造第二個聲音。yet 後面三個症狀並排，讀者只要中一個就會坐直。
swaps: We aligned in Q1 (on paper), yet [症狀].
Everyone said yes—and yet [症狀1] and [症狀2] keep happening.
cards.episode: How to debug a team that isn’t working: the Waterline Model

cards.pattern: These mistakes are invisible until [後果 A], or [後果 B].
cards.quote: These mistakes are invisible until a stakeholder asks a question you can't answer, or a decision falls apart three months later.
cards.zh: 這些錯誤是看不見的，直到某個利害關係人問了你答不出來的問題，或某個決策在三個月後垮掉。
cards.why: invisible until 把「還沒發生的痛」寫成已經在倒數的東西，比 could cause problems 有壓迫感得多。兩個後果一個是當場丟臉、一個是延遲爆炸，覆蓋了讀者兩種恐懼。
swaps: This won't show up until [後果].
The cost is invisible now and expensive later: [後果].
cards.episode: How to do AI analysis you can actually trust

cards.pattern: Here's the problem: if you [做了 X] and then don't [做 Y], you're actually [更糟的結果] than if you had never [做 X] at all.
cards.quote: Here's the problem: if you ask someone to give you their precious time and feedback and then don't act on it, you're actually burning more trust than if you had never asked at all.
cards.zh: 問題在這裡：如果你請人花寶貴時間給你回饋，卻不採取行動，你其實比從來沒問過還更傷信任。
cards.why: Here's the problem: 是英文文件裡把讀者注意力硬拉回來的信號詞。後半的 more X than if you had never...at all 是反直覺結構，證明「什麼都不做」有時反而比較好，說服力很強。
swaps: Here's the catch: [反直覺後果].
Doing this halfway is worse than not doing it: [原因].
cards.episode: What 5 years at Reddit taught us about building for a highly opinionated user base

cards.pattern: We realized that the root cause of nearly all [問題類別] is very simple: [根本原因].
cards.quote: We realized that the root cause of nearly all bad planning processes is very simple: a basic lack of understanding of roles — who is responsible for what, when.
cards.zh: 我們發現幾乎所有糟糕的規劃流程，根本原因都很簡單：大家對角色沒有基本共識——誰在什麼時候該負責什麼。
cards.why: is very simple: 這個冒號前的鋪陳製造了一秒懸念，讀者一定會讀冒號後面。破折號再把抽象名詞翻成白話（who is responsible for what, when），確保沒有人誤解。
swaps: The root cause turns out to be simple: [原因].
Underneath all of these is one thing: [原因].
cards.episode: The Secret to a Great Planning Process — Lessons from Airbnb and Eventbrite

cards.pattern: We had established [A], [B], and [C], but [對象] were still confused about why [D].
cards.quote: We had established our product roadmap and success metrics and our mission and vision, but teams were still confused about why we were working on the projects we chose.
cards.zh: 我們的產品路線圖、成功指標、使命和願景都定好了，但團隊還是搞不懂我們為什麼在做這些專案。
cards.why: 先把「我們該做的都做了」列出來再說 but，讀者才不會以為問題出在偷懶。這是提出新提案前最有用的鋪陳：證明現有工具不夠，而不是沒人用。
swaps: We already have [A] and [B], and yet [問題] persists.
This isn't for lack of [既有努力]—[問題] still happens.
cards.episode: Strategy Blocks: An operator’s guide to product strategy

cards.pattern: Every [角色] obsesses over [顯眼的東西], yet almost no one masters [真正的槓桿]: [X].
cards.quote: Every PM building with generative AI obsesses over crafting better prompts and using the latest LLM, yet almost no one masters the hidden lever behind every exceptional AI product: evaluations.
cards.zh: 每個做生成式 AI 的 PM 都在鑽研怎麼寫更好的 prompt、用最新的模型，卻幾乎沒人練成每個頂尖 AI 產品背後那個隱形槓桿：evals。
cards.why: everyone does X, yet almost no one does Y 是「機會缺口」的萬用句型，同時暗示讀者現在站在多數人那邊（不舒服）而你要帶他去少數人那邊。冒號留到最後才揭曉主題，張力拉滿。
swaps: Everyone is optimizing [X]; almost nobody is touching [Y].
The attention is all on [X]. The leverage is in [Y].
cards.episode: Beyond vibe checks: A PM’s complete guide to evals

cards.pattern: In this [文件], I won't cover [排除的東西], though they're [承認其重要性]. Instead, I want to cover [真正的範圍].
cards.quote: In this post, I won't cover traditional health tips (exercise, get eight hours of sleep, etc.), though they're crucial. Instead, I want to cover some of the lesser-known health gotchas that consistently sap your health.
cards.zh: 這篇我不會談傳統的健康建議（運動、睡滿八小時之類），雖然那些很重要。我想談的是那些比較少人提、卻持續在耗損你健康的細節。
cards.why: 先排除、再加一句 though they're crucial 承認被排除的東西有價值，讀者就不會覺得你在偷懶或無知。這個「排除＋致敬＋改談」三拍是寫 non-goals 最安全的句型。
swaps: I'm not covering [X] here—not because it doesn't matter, but because [理由].
Out of scope for this doc: [X]. In scope: [Y].
cards.episode: A builder’s guide to living a long and healthy life

cards.pattern: Below, I will focus on [A], [B], and [C]. The fourth, [D], is an equally valid focus area, but not one I'd suggest starting with, due to [理由].
cards.quote: The fourth, retention/expansion, is an equally valid focus area, but not one I'd suggest starting with, due to the complexity and effort required to improve those metrics.
cards.zh: 第四項——留存與擴張——同樣是合理的著力點，只是我不建議從它開始，因為要改善這些指標的複雜度和投入都太高。
cards.why: an equally valid ... but not one I'd suggest starting with 是排除選項時最有風度的講法：不貶低它，只講排序理由。due to 後面給出可檢驗的原因，別人要反對就得反對那個原因，而不是反對你的判斷。
swaps: [D] is worth doing—just not first, because [理由].
We're deferring [D] to [時間點] for [理由], not because it's unimportant.
cards.episode: Five steps to starting your product-led growth motion

cards.quote: Several areas that should explicitly *not* be the focus
cards.zh: 幾個明確「不」列為重點的領域。
cards.why: explicitly not 這兩個字是策略文件的分水嶺——沒寫下來的排除等於沒排除。放進「一份好策略包含什麼」的清單裡，等於把非目標升格成必填欄位。
swaps: Explicitly out of scope: [X], [Y].
Areas we are deliberately not investing in this cycle.
cards.pmNote: 好策略必含三塊：3–5 個重點領域、明確不做的領域、以及為什麼這樣選。
cards.episode: Strategy Blocks: An operator’s guide to product strategy

cards.pattern: [X] exists to force a disciplined choice to deploy scarce resources for maximum impact.
cards.quote: Strategy exists to force a disciplined choice to deploy scarce resources for maximum impact.
cards.zh: 策略存在的目的，就是逼出一個有紀律的選擇：把稀缺資源投到影響力最大的地方。
cards.why: exists to 這個說法把一份文件的存在理由講死，適合放在目標段落最前面當定調句。force a disciplined choice 直接暗示「這份文件會讓人不舒服」，先幫讀者做好心理準備。
swaps: The point of this doc is to force one choice, not to list options.
This exists to make a tradeoff explicit.
cards.episode: Strategy Blocks: An operator’s guide to product strategy

cards.pattern: They super-specifically define what success looks like when [X] ships, at first to [用途1], and later to [用途2].
cards.quote: They super-specifically define what success looks like when the product or feature ships, at first to make sure it's even worth doing, and later to help everyone make tradeoff decisions throughout the project.
cards.zh: 它們會超級具體地定義產品或功能上線時「成功長什麼樣」——一開始是為了確認這件事到底值不值得做，之後則是幫大家在專案途中做取捨。
cards.why: at first to... and later to... 把同一段文字的兩種用途分時說明，讀者才知道成功指標不是寫給老闆看的裝飾。這也是說服團隊認真寫成功條件最有效的理由。
swaps: Success criteria serve two jobs: [用途1] now, [用途2] later.
We define this up front so we can cut scope later without re-arguing.
cards.episode: Examples and templates of 1-Pagers and PRDs

cards.pattern: There's a clear (proposed) timeline by which to [動作1], [動作2], and [動作3], to keep the project moving forward (and from exploding in scope).
cards.quote: There's a clear (proposed) timeline by which to review, align on, build and ship the project, to keep the project moving forward (and from exploding in scope).
cards.zh: 有一條明確的（提議中的）時程表，涵蓋審閱、對齊、開發到上線，好讓專案一直往前走（也不至於範圍爆炸）。
cards.why: (proposed) 這個括號是關鍵：把時程標成提議而非命令，別人才敢提意見而不是直接無視。結尾括號補上「不要範圍爆炸」的第二個目的，語氣輕但立場明確。
swaps: Proposed dates below—push back if these don't work.
Timeline (draft) so we don't let this drift.
cards.episode: Examples and templates of 1-Pagers and PRDs

cards.quote: You want your goal to motivate your team to push beyond what's comfortable, but never make it feel impossible.
cards.zh: 你要讓目標推著團隊跨出舒適圈，但絕不能讓人覺得根本做不到。
cards.why: beyond what's comfortable / never feel impossible 用兩個邊界夾出目標的合理區間，比 be ambitious but realistic 這種老套說法具體。談 OKR 目標值時可以整句照用。
swaps: Ambitious enough to stretch, not so far that people stop trying.
Goals should feel uncomfortable, but not impossible.
cards.pmNote: Brian Chesky 的原話：目標應該讓人「不舒服，但不是不可能」。
cards.episode: Setting goals

cards.pattern: If you don't think a metric makes sense for [目標], write out what concretely the world would look like if this was a big success. Make that the success criteria.
cards.quote: If you don't think a metric makes sense for your goal (think long and hard about this), write out what concretely the world would look like if this was a big success. Make that the success criteria.
cards.zh: 如果你覺得這個目標找不到合適的指標（先認真想過再說），那就把「大成功時世界會長什麼樣」具體寫下來，拿那個當成功條件。
cards.why: 括號裡的 (think long and hard about this) 是預先擋掉偷懶的人——先給退路又先堵住濫用，寫給下屬看的文件很好用。Make that the success criteria. 短句收尾，指令感清楚。
swaps: If there's no clean metric, describe what "done well" looks like and use that.
Where we can't measure it, we'll define success qualitatively: [描述].
cards.episode: Setting goals

cards.pattern: Try hard to make it a concrete number, e.g., [X]% increase in [A], [Y]% decrease in [B], [Z]% adoption of [C] within [時間].
cards.quote: Try hard to make it a concrete number, e.g., 10% increase in X, 50% decrease in Y, 20% adoption of feature Z within 3 months.
cards.zh: 盡量把它變成一個具體數字，例如：X 提升 10%、Y 下降 50%、功能 Z 在三個月內達到 20% 採用率。
cards.why: e.g., 後面連給三個不同形狀的例子（增加／減少／採用率＋期限），讀者不必再問「要多具體」。Try hard to 保留了做不到時的空間，不會變成硬性規定。
swaps: Target: [指標] from [現況] to [目標] by [日期].
Where possible, state it as a number and a date.
cards.episode: Setting goals

cards.pattern: [X] is obviously beyond the scope of this [文件].
cards.quote: Learning how to code is obviously beyond the scope of this post.
cards.zh: 學會寫程式顯然超出這篇文章的範圍。
cards.why: beyond the scope of this doc 是英文文件裡最省事的邊界宣告，一句話擋掉整類「那這個呢」的留言。obviously 讓這個排除聽起來理所當然而不是逃避。
swaps: [X] is out of scope here.
We're not covering [X] in this doc.
cards.episode: The top 5 things PMs should know about engineering

cards.pattern: This alone is a deep topic that deserves its own [文件], but a simple heuristic you can use here is [簡化版].
cards.quote: This alone is a deep topic that deserves its own post, but a simple heuristic you can use here is to compare your offering to what else is out there.
cards.zh: 光這一項就是個值得單獨寫一篇的深水區，但你在這裡可以先用一個簡單的判準：把你的產品跟市面上其他選擇比一比。
cards.why: 承認議題很深、明說要另外處理，同時當場給一個夠用的替代方案——讀者不會覺得被打發。deserves its own post/doc 是把範圍縮小又不減損議題重要性的萬用句。
swaps: [X] deserves its own doc; for now we'll use [簡化版].
Full treatment of [X] is a separate exercise—here's the shortcut we'll use.
cards.episode: How to Kickstart and Scale a Marketplace Business – Part 4: Cracking the Chicken-and-Egg Problem 🐣 - Growing Initial Demand (plus a Bonus!)

cards.quote: Situation: What is the state of affairs today? What are the facts that everyone will agree with?
cards.zh: 情境：今天的狀況是什麼？有哪些是大家都會同意的事實？
cards.why: facts that everyone will agree with 給了背景段一個明確的驗收標準：只放沒有人會反對的東西。這一招能避免背景段偷渡立場，讀者一路點頭讀到你的主張。
swaps: Where things stand today: [沒有爭議的事實].
Context (things I think we all agree on): [事實].
cards.pmNote: SCR = Situation（現況）、Complication（變化）、Resolution（建議）。
cards.episode: The Minto Pyramid Principle and the SCR Framework

cards.pattern: In [先前的文件], [誰] and I shared [做過的事]. But we didn't get very concrete about [缺口]. So I thought I'd do a follow-up on this.
cards.quote: But we didn't get very concrete about how to go about nailing down your actual activation metrics. So I thought I'd do a follow-up post on this.
cards.zh: 但我們並沒有很具體地講到，實際上該怎麼把啟用指標定下來。所以我想做一篇後續。
cards.why: 先指認自己前一份文件的缺口，再說明這份文件存在的理由——讀者立刻知道兩份文件的關係，也知道不必回頭讀。So I thought I'd 是英文書面裡最自然的動機交代法。
swaps: The [先前文件] covered [A]; it didn't cover [B]. This doc does.
Following up on [文件] with the part we left open: [缺口].
cards.episode: How to determine your activation metric

cards.pattern: It's particularly hard to [做某事], in part because [次要原因], but mostly because [主要原因].
cards.quote: It's particularly hard to find real-life examples of great 1-Pagers and PRDs, in part because honestly most of them aren't very good, but mostly because these documents have confidential information in them and thus aren't readily shared.
cards.zh: 要找到真實世界裡寫得好的一頁式文件或 PRD 特別難，一部分是因為老實說大多數寫得不怎麼樣，但主要是因為這類文件有機密資訊，不會外流。
cards.why: in part because... but mostly because... 把多個原因排出權重，讀者知道哪個才是真的卡點。只列 because A and B 的寫法會讓讀者自己去猜輕重，通常猜錯。
swaps: This is slow partly because [次因], but mainly because [主因].
Two reasons, in order of weight: [主因], and to a lesser extent [次因].
cards.episode: Examples and templates of 1-Pagers and PRDs

cards.pattern: Over the past [N] years, I've used [X] in [N] different high-stake contexts, at companies large and small.
cards.quote: Over the past 10 years, I've used Strategy Blocks in six different high-stake contexts, at companies large and small.
cards.zh: 過去十年，我在六個高風險情境、大小公司都用過 Strategy Blocks。
cards.why: 用「年數＋次數＋公司規模跨度」三個數字建立可信度，比 I have a lot of experience with this 有力太多。high-stake 一詞暗示這不是紙上談兵。
swaps: We've run this [N] times across [情境], including [例子].
This is the [N]th time I've done this at [規模].
cards.episode: Strategy Blocks: An operator’s guide to product strategy

cards.pattern: After years of [做某事], I've noticed something surprising: [觀察].
cards.quote: After years of building AI products, I've noticed something surprising:
cards.zh: 做了這麼多年 AI 產品之後，我注意到一件出乎意料的事：
cards.why: 資歷（After years of）＋反直覺承諾（something surprising）＋冒號，三個元素合起來讓讀者非讀下一句不可。這是把個人背景轉成閱讀動力最短的寫法。
swaps: After [N] cycles of [X], one thing keeps showing up: [觀察].
Something we didn't expect kept happening: [觀察].
cards.episode: Beyond vibe checks: A PM’s complete guide to evals

cards.pattern: Everyone's [做某事]. But everyone's also getting [壞結果]: [具體症狀1], [症狀2], and [症狀3].
cards.quote: Everyone's "analyzing" customer data with AI. But everyone's also getting answers full of slop: hallucinations, wrong conclusions, and "insights" that just parrot back what you already told it.
cards.zh: 大家都在用 AI「分析」客戶資料。但大家拿到的也都是一堆垃圾：幻覺、錯誤結論，還有只是把你剛餵進去的東西再吐一遍的「洞察」。
cards.why: Everyone's X. But everyone's also Y. 用同一個句型重複兩次，第二次翻轉，節奏本身就在做論證。"analyzing" 的引號是書面英文的反諷手段——沒有語氣時，引號就是你的白眼。
swaps: Everyone is shipping [X]. Almost nobody is checking [Y].
We've all adopted [X]. What we haven't dealt with is [Y].
cards.episode: How to do AI analysis you can actually trust

cards.pattern: We've both been there, over and over again, while [具體經歷].
cards.quote: We (Tal and Aman) have both been there, over and over again while building AI products for tens of thousands of customers.
cards.zh: 我們（Tal 和 Aman）都經歷過，而且一而再再而三，就在替數萬名客戶打造 AI 產品的過程中。
cards.why: 先站到讀者同一邊（been there）再亮資歷，順序反過來就變成炫耀。over and over again 讓「我也犯過」聽起來誠實而不是客套。
swaps: We've made this mistake ourselves, more than once, while [經歷].
This isn't hypothetical for us—we hit it during [專案].
cards.episode: How to build AI product sense

cards.pattern: (To be clear, [避免誤讀的澄清].)
cards.quote: (To be clear, these layers are metaphorical and don't correspond exactly to org structure.)
cards.zh: （先講清楚，這些層級是比喻，並不完全對應到組織架構。）
cards.why: 整句放進括號，等於在正文旁邊加一條註腳而不打斷敘事節奏。文件會被轉發給沒上下文的人，這種當場拆彈的括號能省掉之後一整串誤會。
swaps: (Note: [澄清]—this is not a proposal to [誤讀].)
(For the avoidance of doubt: [澄清].)
cards.episode: How Notion builds product

cards.pattern: Write "[Hit/Shipped/Cut] [具體標的] [量化條件]", not "[Held/Attended/Went to] [活動]".
cards.quote: For example, write “Hit team’s goals” and “Shipped project X on time and under budget," not “Held a great meeting” or “Went to three conferences."
cards.zh: 舉例來說，要寫「達成團隊目標」「專案 X 準時且在預算內出貨」，而不是「開了一場很棒的會」或「參加了三場研討會」。
cards.why: 自評的第一條規則全在動詞上：hit / shipped 落在結果，held / went to 落在活動。台灣人習慣寫「參與了」「協助了」，在英文 review 裡那叫 attendance record，不叫 impact。
swaps: Delivered [專案] two weeks ahead of schedule.
Cut [指標] from [A] to [B] in [期間].
cards.pmNote: 履歷、自評、升遷案共用同一條線：activity ≠ impact。
cards.episode: The Power of Performance Reviews: Use This System to Become a Better Manager 🤝

cards.pattern: I led [專案], which spanned [跨部門範圍], reported up to [層級], and became [對公司策略的意義].
cards.quote: I got promoted from a mid-level PM (L5) to a Senior PM (L6) after leading a mission-critical project (Instant Book) for a couple of years, which spanned multiple departments, reported up to the executive staff, and became a major part of the company strategy
cards.zh: 我從中階 PM（L5）升到資深 PM（L6），是因為我帶了兩年一個關鍵任務級的專案（Instant Book）——它橫跨多個部門、直接向高階主管層匯報，最後成為公司策略的重要一環。
cards.why: 三個並列子句把「一個專案」翻譯成三種能被 calibration 認可的 scope 訊號：橫向廣度（spanned）、縱向能見度（reported up to）、策略權重（became）。中文寫「我負責一個很重要的專案」在英語職場等於什麼都沒說。
swaps: I owned [專案], which touched [N] teams and reported into [誰].
[專案] cut across [A]、[B] and [C], and fed directly into [年度目標].
cards.pmNote: calibration 是主管們互相比對部屬表現的會議——你的自評會在那個房間被讀出來。
cards.episode: How to get promoted

cards.pattern: As [公司指標] scaled from [A] to [B], I led [團隊/工作] tackling everything from [X], to [Y], to [Z].
cards.quote: As the number of homes on Airbnb scaled from around 100,000 in 2012 to over 6 million today, I led teams tackling everything from supply growth, to guest booking conversion, to marketplace quality.
cards.zh: 在 Airbnb 房源數從 2012 年的約十萬成長到今天的六百萬以上的這段期間，我帶的團隊處理過各種題目：供給成長、旅客訂房轉換、到市集品質。
cards.why: 先把公司的成長曲線當背景，再把自己放進去——「我的工作發生在這條曲線上」比「我做了 A、B、C」有份量得多，而且完全沒有一句自誇。
swaps: Over the period [公司指標] grew from [A] to [B], I owned [範圍].
During [階段], I led work spanning [X], [Y], and [Z].
cards.episode: 28 Ways to Grow Supply in a Marketplace 📈

cards.pattern: I realized that [A] performed worse than [B], resulting in [把落差換算成使用者或營收的量體].
cards.quote: in my first months at Slack, I realized that user onboarding on mobile performed worse than on web, resulting in hundreds of thousands of people who were signing up without experiencing Slack’s magical value of seamless team communication
cards.zh: 在 Slack 的頭幾個月，我發現行動版的新手引導表現比網頁版差，結果是有幾十萬人註冊了卻從來沒體驗到 Slack 那個「團隊溝通無縫接軌」的核心價值。
cards.why: 「發現一個問題」本身不值錢，值錢的是把落差換算成規模（hundreds of thousands of people）。resulting in 這個分詞句讓因果看起來像事實陳述，不像在邀功。
swaps: I found that [A] lagged [B] by [N%], resulting in [量體].
[指標] on [平台 A] was [N%] below [平台 B], which meant [後果].
cards.episode: How to make an impact in your first 90 days

cards.pattern: So I identified [機會] and shipped [動作] that increased [指標].
cards.quote: So I identified opportunities to simplify the mobile onboarding flow and shipped a quick experiment that increased user activation.
cards.zh: 所以我找出可以簡化行動版新手流程的地方，並且很快出了一個實驗，讓使用者啟用率提升。
cards.why: 自評的黃金三段：問題→我做的事→指標動了，一句話寫完，讀者不必自己推論。identified 和 shipped 兩個動詞並列，同時展現判斷力與執行力。
swaps: So I scoped [問題] and shipped [方案] that moved [指標] by [N%].
I identified [機會] and ran [實驗] that lifted [指標].
cards.episode: How to make an impact in your first 90 days

cards.pattern: To solve for [問題], I introduced [做法], which [對人或流程的效果].
cards.quote: To solve for higher shipping velocity, I introduced Demo Power Hour, which helped everyone feel ownership and pride in their work. To solve for transparency and accountability, I introduced Scorecard.
cards.zh: 為了解決出貨速度的問題，我導入了 Demo Power Hour，這讓每個人對自己的工作更有擁有感和成就感。為了解決透明度和當責的問題，我導入了 Scorecard。
cards.why: 整段自評最好用的骨架：To solve for X, I introduced Y, which Z——重複兩三次就變成一份有節奏的清單。每一條都自帶「我為什麼做」，不用另外解釋。
swaps: To address [問題], I set up [機制], which [效果].
To solve for [問題], I built [工具] that [結果].
cards.episode: How to make an impact in your first 90 days

cards.pattern: At [公司], I [果斷動詞] [N%] of [東西] to [目的] and consolidated around [留下來的少數幾件事].
cards.quote: At Linktree, I axed 50% of meetings to create more maker time and consolidated around just a few key rituals.
cards.zh: 在 Linktree，我砍掉了一半的會議，好挪出更多真正做事的時間，只保留幾個關鍵的固定儀式。
cards.why: 「砍掉」也是成果。axed 這種果斷動詞加上百分比，把減法寫成了決策力；後半句 consolidated around 補上「我不是亂砍，我留下了什麼」，避免顯得魯莽。
swaps: I cut [N%] of [東西] to free up [資源].
I retired [舊做法] and consolidated around [新做法].
cards.episode: How to make an impact in your first 90 days

cards.pattern: Later, at [公司], I [動詞] across teams to overhaul [範圍], enabling it to [新的能力].
cards.quote: Later, at Google, I negotiated across teams to overhaul YouTube’s infrastructure, design, and policies, enabling it to support high-profile TV content like NFL Sunday Ticket.
cards.zh: 後來在 Google，我跨團隊協調，把 YouTube 的基礎架構、設計和政策全面翻修，讓它能夠支援像 NFL Sunday Ticket 這種重量級電視內容。
cards.why: enabling it to... 這個分詞尾巴是自評的高招：把你做的技術工作接到一個外部世界看得懂的結果上。少了它，「翻修基礎架構」只是苦工。
swaps: I worked across [N] teams to rebuild [系統], enabling us to [新能力].
I aligned [A] and [B] to overhaul [X], which made [Y] possible.
cards.episode: A PM’s guide to influence

cards.pattern: To do that, I spearheaded a [有爭議的/高風險的] project to experiment with [新做法].
cards.quote: To do that, I spearheaded a controversial project to experiment with a new approach to free-to-paid conversion.
cards.zh: 為了達成這件事，我主導了一個具爭議性的專案，去試驗一種全新的免費轉付費做法。
cards.why: spearheaded 比 led 多了「我是那個先站出來的人」的重量；主動寫出 controversial，等於在說「這件事本來沒人想碰」——難度是可以自己標注的，而且標了才算數。
swaps: I spearheaded [專案] despite [阻力].
I took on [沒人想碰的題目] and drove it to [結果].
cards.episode: A PM’s guide to influence

cards.pattern: I framed [提案] around [對方在乎的角度] rather than emphasizing [我方的目標].
cards.quote: I framed the entire proposal around the benefits it would have for users (the CEO’s POV) rather than emphasizing the revenue impact of the project (our team’s goal).
cards.zh: 我把整份提案的框架建立在「這對使用者有什麼好處」（執行長的視角），而不是強調這個專案的營收影響（我們團隊的目標）。
cards.why: 自評裡最難寫的是「判斷力」。這句用 A rather than B 的對照，把一個看不見的決定變成可觀察的動作，讀的人自己就會得出「這人懂得看場合」的結論。
swaps: I positioned [X] around [他們的目標] instead of [我們的目標].
Rather than leading with [數字], I framed it around [對方的痛點].
cards.pmNote: 把提案掛在決策者的世界觀上，是 influence without authority 的核心動作。
cards.episode: A PM’s guide to influence

cards.pattern: At [公司], my responsibilities grew from [起點] to [終點]. Along the way, I helped create [成果], including [列舉].
