cards.quote: At Amazon, my responsibilities grew from an initial team of six to more than 800. Along the way, I helped create household products you would recognize, including Prime Video, Kindle, Alexa, Twitch, and Prime Gaming.
cards.zh: 在 Amazon，我負責的範圍從一開始的六人團隊成長到八百多人。這一路上，我參與打造了幾個大家都認得的產品，包括 Prime Video、Kindle、Alexa、Twitch 和 Prime Gaming。
cards.why: 兩個把自誇降溫的技巧同時出現：responsibilities grew（範圍成長，主詞不是我）跟 helped create（參與而非獨力）。數字自己會說話，動詞就可以放軟。
swaps: My scope grew from [A] to [B] over [期間].
I helped build [產品], including [列舉].
cards.episode: The Magic Loop

cards.pattern: In aggregate, [一系列小動作] led to a [X%] increase in [指標] at [公司].
cards.quote: In aggregate, title tag experiments led to a 15-20% increase in traffic at Airbnb
cards.zh: 整體加總起來，標題標籤的一系列實驗讓 Airbnb 的流量成長了 15 到 20%。
cards.why: In aggregate 是自評神句：把一堆單看不起眼的小改動合法地加總成一個大數字，同時暗示「這不是一次性的運氣，是一套持續的做法」。
swaps: Taken together, these changes drove a [X%] lift in [指標].
Across [N] experiments, we saw a cumulative [X%] improvement in [指標].
cards.episode: How to run SEO experiments

cards.pattern: The [最好的 X] I [led/built] actually had more [反直覺特徵], not less. We’d [做法], and it made [結果].
cards.quote: The highest-performing teams I led actually had more conflict, not less. We’d institutionalized productive disagreement, and it made our decisions faster
cards.zh: 我帶過表現最好的團隊，衝突其實是更多、不是更少。我們把「有建設性的意見不合」制度化了，結果是決策速度變快。
cards.why: 用「反直覺 + 我的親身樣本」寫自評，比一堆形容詞有效十倍。actually...not less 的對照句把你的判斷寫成了證據；that made 收尾又把它落回到可衡量的結果。
swaps: The [X] that worked best actually had less [常見做法], not more.
Counterintuitively, [做法 A] outperformed [做法 B] on [指標].
cards.pmNote: 面試與自評都吃這種 spiky POV：只有你的樣本能得出的結論。
cards.episode: How to use AI for your next job interview

cards.pattern: ...that includes the outcomes you drove and the impact on [公司/團隊目標].
cards.quote: Write a detailed self-review (do this in parallel with writing your coverage plan) that includes the outcomes you drove and the impact on the company’s goals.
cards.zh: 寫一份詳細的自評（跟你的職務代理計畫同步進行），內容要包含你推動出來的結果，以及它對公司目標的影響。
cards.why: outcomes you drove 跟 impact on the company's goals 是兩層：前者是你的動作造成的結果，後者是公司在乎的事。只寫前者叫交代，兩層都寫才叫自評。
swaps: ...covering the outcomes I drove and how they moved [公司目標].
...the results I delivered and their impact on [年度 OKR].
cards.pmNote: 台灣人自評最常見的缺口就在第二層：做了什麼寫得很細，對公司有什麼用完全沒接上。
cards.episode: How to create an exceptional coverage plan for your parental leave

cards.pattern: I noticed [問題]. I went ahead and fixed that by [動名詞].
cards.quote: I noticed we often miss vacations in our schedules. I went ahead and fixed that by adding a step to solicit and document holiday plans with the team.
cards.zh: 我注意到我們排程時常常漏掉休假。我就直接處理掉了——加了一個步驟，去跟團隊收集並記錄假期規劃。
cards.why: went ahead and 是「我沒等你叫我做」的標準寫法，語氣輕但訊息重。這兩句可以直接貼進週報，它同時報告了你的觀察力跟自主性。
swaps: I noticed [問題], so I went ahead and [動作].
This kept coming up, so I put [機制] in place.
cards.pmNote: 在英語職場，「主動補洞」比「把交辦的事做好」更容易換到 scope。
cards.episode: The Magic Loop

cards.pattern: [X] don’t get [結果] for [做好本分]. They get [結果] by demonstrating [更大的潛力].
cards.quote: People don’t get promoted for doing their jobs really well. They get promoted by demonstrating their potential to do more.
cards.zh: 人不會因為把本分做得很好而升遷。他們是因為展現出「能做更多」的潛力而升遷。
cards.why: not A, but B 的兩句式對比是英語職場論證的骨架。第二句用 demonstrating（展現給人看）而不是 having（擁有）——這正是台灣人自評最缺的那個動詞。
swaps: It’s not enough to [做好本分]; you have to demonstrate [下一階的能力].
[X] isn’t rewarded for [A]—it’s rewarded for [B].
cards.episode: How to get promoted

cards.pattern: Development areas include [名詞化能力 1], [動名詞 2], and more [形容詞] [名詞 3].
cards.quote: A few examples of potential development areas include reliable execution, increasing code quality, and more succinct verbal communication.
cards.zh: 可能的發展方向舉例來說有：穩定的執行力、提升程式碼品質、以及更精簡的口頭溝通。
cards.why: 把弱點寫成「發展方向」的名詞短語（reliable execution），而不是自貶的句子（I'm not good at execution）。名詞化讓缺點聽起來像一個可調整的參數，而不是一個人格缺陷。
swaps: My focus for next cycle is [名詞化能力].
The area I’m actively working on is [名詞短語].
cards.pmNote: development area 是英語 review 的固定詞；別寫 weakness，那個詞在書面上留下的痕跡太重。
cards.episode: The Power of Performance Reviews: Use This System to Become a Better Manager 🤝

cards.pattern: A simple story arc: [起點對照] → [本期表現] → [下一步的重點].
cards.quote: I try to make a simple story arc, starting by describing how far they’ve come, then a sentence or two about how they did this cycle, and ending on a high-level overview of what they need to focus on next.
cards.zh: 我會盡量做出一個簡單的故事弧線：先描述這個人走了多遠，再用一兩句講他這個週期表現如何，最後用一段高層次的說明收在「接下來要專注什麼」。
cards.why: 自評與主管評語共用同一個結構。台灣人寫自評常只有中間那段（這期做了什麼），少了「我從哪裡走過來」跟「我下一步要往哪」，讀起來像交差不像成長。
swaps: Coming into this cycle I was [起點]; this cycle I [表現]; next I’ll focus on [方向].
A year ago I couldn’t [X]. This cycle I [Y]. Next cycle I want to [Z].
cards.episode: The Power of Performance Reviews: Use This System to Become a Better Manager 🤝

cards.pattern: This ended up [負面後果] (as it should have), and it taught me [教訓].
cards.quote: This ended up hurting my performance review (as it should have), and it taught me the lesson that perception matters heavily in the PM role.
cards.zh: 這件事最後確實拖累了我的績效考核（本來就應該），也讓我學到一課：在 PM 這個角色，別人怎麼看你，份量非常重。
cards.why: (as it should have) 這個插入語是整句的關鍵：主動承認懲罰是公平的，你就從被評價者變成了評價者。在書面自評裡承認失誤而不自貶，靠的就是這種語氣控制。
swaps: That cost us [代價], and fairly so—it taught me [教訓].
I got that wrong, and the feedback was warranted; what I took from it was [教訓].
cards.episode: How to know if you're doing a good job as a product manager

cards.pattern: a list of times you’ve made an impact at [X] — include metrics, screenshots, timelines, stories.
cards.quote: Go open up a new doc and start dumping a list of times you’ve made an impact at your current job. Include metrics, screenshots, timelines, stories—anything that’ll help you tell the story of your successes.
cards.zh: 開一份新文件，把你在現在這份工作上做出影響力的每個時刻通通倒進去。放進數據、截圖、時間軸、故事——任何能幫你把成功講成一個故事的東西。
cards.why: times you've made an impact 這個名詞化寫法很好用——把抽象的「影響力」變成可以逐條列舉的事件。tell the story of your successes 則提醒：自評是敘事，不是清單。
swaps: Keep a running doc of times you moved [指標].
Log every win with the metric, the date, and who else was involved.
cards.pmNote: 英文圈叫這份文件 brag document；平常不寫，年底就只剩印象。
cards.episode: How to be prepared for layoffs

cards.pattern: When you’re working independently, [誰] won’t see [你做對的事] and [你克服的困難].
cards.quote: When you’re working independently, your manager won’t see all of the great decisions you make and the tough challenges you overcome.
cards.zh: 當你獨立作業的時候，你的主管不會看到你做的那些好決定，也不會看到你克服的那些難題。
cards.why: 這句是台灣讀者最該內化的一句。它不是在教你吹牛，是在陳述一個結構事實：能見度是有物理限制的。承認這件事，寫自評就從「炫耀」變成「補資訊」。
swaps: Most of this happened out of view, so I’m writing it down here.
Since this ran async, I want to surface the calls I made along the way.
cards.episode: Becoming a senior Product Manager

cards.pattern: a simple weekly "[名稱]" email to your boss with (1) [目前優先序], (2) [心上的事], (3) [需要幫忙的卡點].
cards.quote: I suggest sending a simple weekly “State of The Me” email to your boss with (1) your current priorities, (2) things on your mind, and (3) blockers you need help with.
cards.zh: 我建議每週寄一封簡單的「State of The Me」信給你的主管，內容包含：(1) 你目前的優先事項、(2) 你心上在想的事、(3) 你需要幫忙排除的卡點。
cards.why: 自評不是一年一次的事，是五十二週的累積。這個三欄結構之所以好用，是因為第三欄（blockers）讓這封信對主管有價值——不然它只是你的日記。
swaps: Weekly update: priorities / open questions / where I need help.
Here’s where things stand, what I’m chewing on, and what I need from you.
cards.pmNote: 這封信年底會變成你自評的原始素材庫。
cards.episode: Managing up

cards.pattern: I want us to [共同目標] so we can [好處]. [具體場合], you [具體行為], which I [我自己的疏失].
cards.quote: I want us to reduce handoff friction so we can ship faster. The last handoff meeting we had, you didn’t share any background customer research, which I failed to flag at the time.
cards.zh: 我希望我們可以減少交接時的摩擦，這樣才能出貨更快。上次交接會議你沒有分享任何背景的使用者研究，而我當下也沒有提出來。
cards.why: 兩句話做了三件事：先把回饋掛在「我們共同想要的東西」上、再講可查證的具體場合與行為（不是形容詞）、最後主動認領自己的一份責任。第三段最少人做，但最能解除對方防衛。
swaps: I want us to [目標]. In [場合], [行為] — and I should have raised it then.
My goal here is [共同結果]. What I saw was [行為], which I didn’t flag at the time.
cards.pmNote: GAIN 框架：Goal（共同目標）→ Actions（行為）→ Impacts（影響）→ Next actions（下一步）。
cards.episode: Introducing the GAIN framework for feedback: an evidence-based approach to giving feedback that people love, appreciate, and act on

cards.pattern: [缺了什麼] led to [可觀察的後果] instead of [原本該發生的事]. Can you [具體請求] next time?
cards.quote: Lacking that context led to multiple rounds of engineers pinging you with questions instead of making empowered decisions on their own. Can you include that next time?
cards.zh: 少了那個脈絡，結果是工程師一輪又一輪來問你問題，而不是自己就能做出有把握的決定。下次可以把它一起附上嗎？
cards.why: 用 led to 把行為跟後果接起來，讓對方自己得出結論，你不必說「你這樣不對」。結尾一個 yes/no 問句把回饋收束成可執行的動作，而不是懸在空中的抱怨。
swaps: Without [X], [後果] instead of [理想狀況]. Could you [動作] going forward?
That gap led to [具體後果]. Would you be able to [請求] next round?
cards.episode: Introducing the GAIN framework for feedback: an evidence-based approach to giving feedback that people love, appreciate, and act on

cards.pattern: [可量測的行為] averaged [數字] last [期間].
cards.quote: Response times to client emails averaged 4.2 days last month
cards.zh: 上個月回覆客戶信件的時間平均是 4.2 天。
cards.why: 書面回饋會被存檔、被轉發，所以每一句都要禁得起爭辯。這句沒有形容詞、沒有人稱、只有數字——對方可以反駁數字，但沒辦法說你在人身攻擊。對照組是「You're being unprofessional」。
swaps: Over the last quarter, [X] took an average of [N] days.
In [期間], [指標] came in at [數字] against a target of [數字].
cards.pmNote: observation vs judgment 的分界線：能被錄影機拍到的才叫 observation。
cards.episode: Introducing the GAIN framework for feedback: an evidence-based approach to giving feedback that people love, appreciate, and act on

cards.pattern: Right now, I can see you [具體行為清單], and I can only imagine how [對方的感受] that must be.
cards.quote: Right now, I can see you are on every sales call, email, in all of the Slack channels across every team, and I can only imagine how exhausting that must be.
cards.zh: 現在我看到的是：你出現在每一通銷售電話、每一封信、每個團隊的每個 Slack 頻道裡，我只能想像那有多累人。
cards.why: I can see 標記這是觀察不是指控；I can only imagine 把情緒的詮釋權交還給對方，等於邀請他自己說出來。往上給主管或創辦人書面回饋時，這組是最安全的開場。
swaps: From where I sit, you’re [行為清單], and I can imagine that’s [感受].
What I’m seeing is [行為]. I can only imagine how [形容詞] that gets.
cards.episode: Introducing the GAIN framework for feedback: an evidence-based approach to giving feedback that people love, appreciate, and act on

cards.pattern: I imagine that you [對方的動機猜測] because [他自己的理由].
cards.quote: I imagine that you feel like you have to do it because you feel the job won’t get done unless you do.
cards.zh: 我猜你會覺得非做不可，是因為你覺得如果你不做，這件事就不會完成。
cards.why: 先幫對方把「他這麼做的合理理由」講出來，他就不用花力氣自我辯護。I imagine 是安全的猜測標記——猜錯了對方會來修正你，而那正是你要的：他開口了。
swaps: My guess is you [動機], because [理由].
I suspect this comes from [理由]—correct me if I’m off.
cards.episode: Introducing the GAIN framework for feedback: an evidence-based approach to giving feedback that people love, appreciate, and act on

cards.pattern: I think there might be another approach here that could [對他的好處] and, at the same time, [對團隊的好處].
cards.quote: I think there might be another approach here that could create more time for you to focus on the areas where your impact is greatest and, at the same time, help the team step up, do better work, and feel more motivated.
cards.zh: 我覺得這裡可能有另一種做法，一方面可以幫你騰出更多時間去做影響力最大的事，同時也能讓團隊接手、做出更好的成果、更有動力。
cards.why: might / could 這組雙重弱化讓提議不像命令；「對你好 + 同時對團隊好」的雙軌好處，是說服比你資深的人時最有效的框——你不是在要求他改，你是在給他一個更划算的選項。
swaps: There might be a version of this that [對他的好處] while also [對團隊的好處].
I wonder if there’s an approach that gives you [好處] and gives the team [好處].
cards.episode: Introducing the GAIN framework for feedback: an evidence-based approach to giving feedback that people love, appreciate, and act on

cards.pattern: The interesting thing is, though, I know you [正面事實]—[你的證據]—but you still sometimes [行為].
cards.quote: The interesting thing is, though, I know you trust me a lot—you’ve mentioned it, and I’ve even observed it—but you still sometimes do it with me.
cards.zh: 但有趣的是，我知道你很信任我——你講過，我也確實觀察到了——可是你有時候還是會對我這樣。
cards.why: 先舉出對方做對的例外，再指出模式仍在。這讓「你做得到」變成一件已被證明的事，回饋就從指責變成提醒——而且你的證據是他自己的話。
swaps: What’s interesting is that with [情境 A] you already [理想行為]—but with [情境 B] it still [行為].
You’ve done exactly this well before, in [場合]. It just hasn’t carried over to [場合].
cards.episode: Introducing the GAIN framework for feedback: an evidence-based approach to giving feedback that people love, appreciate, and act on

cards.pattern: So moving forward, I’ll [我的動作], you’ll [你的動作], and I’ll [我的第三個動作].
cards.quote: So moving forward, I’ll continue proactively sending you updates, you’ll work on stepping back—i.e. not jumping in or pinging me with status checks—and I’ll name it in the moment if the old pattern rears its head.
cards.zh: 所以接下來：我會繼續主動寄進度更新給你，你會練習退一步——也就是不要跳進來或一直來問狀況——而如果舊習慣又冒出來，我會當下直接講出來。
cards.why: 回饋談完一定要有人把結論寫下來，而且要包含自己的動作。三個主詞交錯出現（I / you / I），讓這件事看起來是雙方的專案，不是你在給他派工。
swaps: To recap: I’ll [動作], you’ll [動作], and we’ll check in on [日期].
Moving forward — me: [動作]. You: [動作]. Both: [動作].
cards.pmNote: Who does What by When（WWW）——沒有這三個要素的回饋，八成不會發生。
cards.episode: Introducing the GAIN framework for feedback: an evidence-based approach to giving feedback that people love, appreciate, and act on

cards.pattern: When you [行為], it [對流程的後果]. Can you [動作] and let me know if there are any blockers?
cards.quote: Hey, when you don’t schedule interviews in the time frame you said you would, it slows down our hiring process. Can you schedule those this week and let me know if there are any blockers?
cards.zh: 嘿，當你沒有在你說的時間內排好面試，我們的招募流程就會被拖慢。可以請你這週把那幾場排掉嗎？有什麼卡住的地方也跟我說。
cards.why: when you...it... 是最短的「行為→影響」句式，短到可以直接放進 Slack。結尾加上 let me know if there are any blockers，把「催進度」變成「我來幫你排除障礙」。
swaps: When [行為] slips, it [後果]. Could you [動作] by [時間]?
When [X] happens, [後果]. Anything blocking you on this?
cards.episode: Introducing the GAIN framework for feedback: an evidence-based approach to giving feedback that people love, appreciate, and act on

cards.quote: I’m giving you these comments because I have very high expectations [challenge] and I know that you can reach them [support].
cards.zh: 我給你這些意見，是因為我對你的期待很高，而且我知道你到得了。
cards.why: 一句話同時放進「標準很高」跟「我相信你到得了」。史丹佛的雙盲對照實驗顯示，加上這一句的回饋讓學生的修改量變成四倍，改動品質也高出 26%——這是投報率最高的一句話。
swaps: I’m being this direct because I think you can clear a much higher bar.
I wouldn’t bother writing this if I didn’t think you could get there.
cards.pmNote: 原文的 [challenge] 與 [support] 是作者標注的兩個功能，實際寫的時候不用寫出來。
cards.episode: Introducing the GAIN framework for feedback: an evidence-based approach to giving feedback that people love, appreciate, and act on

cards.pattern: What are 2-3 things [X] should [start / continue / stop] doing? Why?
cards.quote: What are 2-3 things Jane should start doing? Why?
cards.zh: Jane 有哪 2 到 3 件事應該「開始做」？為什麼？
cards.why: start / continue / stop 三分法是英語職場書面回饋的預設骨架。限定數量（2-3）逼對方排序，加一個 Why 逼出理由而不是標籤——沒有 Why，你收到的會是一堆形容詞。
swaps: What are 2-3 things [X] should continue doing? Why?
What are 2-3 things [X] should stop doing? Why?
cards.pmNote: 這三題也可以拿來當自評的自問清單。
cards.episode: The Power of Performance Reviews: Use This System to Become a Better Manager 🤝

cards.pattern: He told me he could see that I was [好意圖], but that I was [具體行為] so much that [對別人的具體後果].
cards.quote: He was nice about it; he told me he could see that I was trying to help and had good intentions, but that I was pestering his engineers about problems so much that they could not focus.
cards.zh: 他講得很客氣：他說他看得出來我是想幫忙、出發點是好的，但我一直去煩他的工程師問問題，煩到他們沒辦法專心。
cards.why: 「先承認對方的意圖是好的，再講行為造成的具體後果」是給書面回饋時最省力的解防衛結構。關鍵在 so much that——它把程度問題講清楚，避免對方以為你要他完全別做。
swaps: I can see the intent behind [行為], but at this volume it [後果].
I know you’re trying to [好意圖]; the effect right now is that [後果].
cards.episode: The Magic Loop

cards.pattern: a personalized document with the projects we worked on together, the impact [I] drove, and the type of feedback you’re looking for
cards.quote: Send them each a personalized document with the projects you worked on together, the impact you drove, and the type of feedback you’re looking for.
cards.zh: 分別寄給每個人一份客製化的文件，裡面寫上你們一起做過的專案、你推動出來的影響，以及你希望他們給哪一類的回饋。
cards.why: 請人幫你背書時，「給素材」比「拜託」有用。三個名詞片語剛好對應對方寫推薦時需要的三件事：共同經驗、可引用的成果、你希望被突顯的面向。
swaps: I’ve pulled together the projects we overlapped on and the outcomes, in case it’s useful.
To make this easy, here’s what we worked on together and what I’d love you to speak to.
cards.pmNote: 英語職場的 peer review 是有截止日的行政作業——你給的素材越好，寫出來的評語越具體。
cards.episode: How to create an exceptional coverage plan for your parental leave

cards.pattern: How can I help you make the case on my behalf?
cards.quote: Ask how you can help your manager make the case on your behalf.
cards.zh: 去問你的主管：你可以怎麼幫他替你講話。
cards.why: make the case on someone's behalf 是升遷與背書的核心動詞片語。把它寫成問句，等於承認決定權在對方，同時把自己變成他的隊友而不是請託人。
swaps: What would help you make the case for me?
Is there anything you need from me to advocate for this?
cards.episode: How to create an exceptional coverage plan for your parental leave

cards.pattern: The most underappreciated ingredient in [X] is to have someone with influence fight for you in [場合].
cards.quote: The most underappreciated, and often the most powerful, ingredient in getting promoted is to have someone with influence fight for you in the calibration process.
cards.zh: 升遷這件事最被低估、往往也最有力的一個要素，是在 calibration 會議上有一個有影響力的人替你力爭。
cards.why: fight for you 是英語職場描述背書的常用動詞，calibration process 則是那個房間的正式名字。台灣讀者要先知道有這個房間，才會理解為什麼「寫下來的評語」那麼重要。
swaps: Having someone senior fight for you in [場合] matters more than people admit.
What moves the needle is a champion in the room when [決策] happens.
cards.pmNote: calibration＝各部門主管把所有人攤在同一張表上比較的會議。你不在場，你寫的字在。
cards.episode: How to get promoted

cards.pattern: He led [量化規模], holds [量化成果], and helped [具名的組織資產].
cards.quote: He led global teams of over 800, holds more than 70 patents, and helped draft one of Amazon’s 14 core Leadership Principles, “Ownership.”
cards.zh: 他帶過超過八百人的全球團隊，擁有七十多項專利，還參與草擬了 Amazon 十四條核心領導準則之一的「Ownership」。
cards.why: 介紹別人（或幫人寫推薦）的黃金結構：三個並列、全部帶數字、最後一項是一個有名字的具體資產。形容詞一個都不需要——數字自己會發出「這個人很強」的訊號。
swaps: She led [規模], shipped [具名成果], and built [具名資產].
He’s scaled [規模], holds [數量] of [X], and authored [具名文件].
cards.episode: The Magic Loop

cards.pattern: the only info I really need are [X], your vouch, and [Y]
cards.quote: The fields are optional, the only info I really need are their skills, your vouch, and your email.
cards.zh: 欄位都是選填的，我真正需要的只有：他的專長、你的背書、還有你的 email。
cards.why: vouch 當名詞用（your vouch＝你的背書）是很道地的縮寫寫法。台灣人只會 recommend，而 vouch for 帶著「我拿自己的信用擔保」的重量——推薦人的成本也被算進去了。
swaps: I can vouch for [X] on [具體面向].
Happy to vouch for her—I worked with her on [專案] for [期間].
cards.episode: Ideal sprint length, designer vs. PM roles, running PM team meetings, running post-mortems, best product/executive coaches, and much more

cards.pattern: He’s especially talented at [具體能力]. We’re super-lucky to have [他] share [什麼] with us.
cards.quote: he’s especially talented at explaining deeply technical subjects clearly and directly. We’re super-lucky to have Justin share his wisdom with us.
cards.zh: 他特別擅長把很硬的技術主題講得又清楚又直接。能請到 Justin 來分享他的智慧，我們真的很幸運。
cards.why: especially talented at + 動名詞，把讚美釘在一個具體技能上，而不是「他很棒」。第二句用 we're lucky 把重心從「他多厲害」轉成「我們受益」——這是英語書面引介人的標準收尾。
swaps: She’s especially strong at [能力]. We’re lucky to have her on [專案].
What [X] does best is [能力]—we’re fortunate to have him involved.
cards.episode: The top 5 things PMs should know about engineering

cards.pattern: Given [模糊的處境], they can [能力] (and drive the work through to [結果]).
cards.quote: Given an ambiguous problem area, they can rapidly pick out the most important problems to solve (and drive the work through to tangible impact).
cards.zh: 丟給他一個模糊的問題領域，他能很快挑出最該解的那幾個問題（而且把工作一路推到看得見的成果）。
cards.why: 背書一個人最有說服力的寫法不是形容他，是描述「給他什麼條件、他會產出什麼」。Given X, they can Y 這個條件句等於在寫一份可驗證的規格。
swaps: Given [不完整的資訊], she can [能力] without [常見的失誤].
Hand him [混亂的狀況] and he’ll come back with [清楚的產出].
cards.episode: Becoming a senior Product Manager

cards.pattern: Shoutout to [人名] ([職稱]), who [具體貢獻] for [期間].
cards.quote: Shoutout to Nico Sacheri (Principal PM) and Hideki Shima (Eng Director), who have been crushing it leading the Connections team for the past couple of years.
cards.zh: 特別點名 Nico Sacheri（首席 PM）和 Hideki Shima（工程總監）——過去這兩年他們把 Connections 團隊帶得非常出色。
cards.why: 公開肯定要有份量，就要有三件事：全名、職稱、做了什麼多久。加上職稱是關鍵——它讓不認識這個人的讀者也知道這個肯定的重量。
swaps: Shoutout to [人名] ([職稱]) for [具體貢獻] over the last [期間].
Special credit to [人名], who has been [動作] since [時間].
cards.episode: How Duolingo reignited user growth

cards.pattern: Credit to [人名] for [動詞 1]、[動詞 2] and [動詞 3] [產出].
cards.quote: Credit to Louise Beryl for designing, analyzing, and articulating the most interesting findings from this (massive) survey.
cards.zh: 功勞要給 Louise Beryl——這份（龐大的）調查的設計、分析，以及把最有意思的發現寫清楚，都是她做的。
cards.why: Credit to X for + 三個並列動名詞，是署名文件裡歸功給別人的標準格式。三個動詞讓貢獻的範圍具體到無法被含糊帶過——這比 thanks to 更有法律感、也更有份量。
swaps: Credit to [人名] for [動名詞] and [動名詞].
The [產出] here is [人名]’s work—I just [我做的小事].
cards.pmNote: 在英語職場，把功勞明確寫給別人不會稀釋你的貢獻，反而會提高你的可信度。
cards.episode: How much do U.S. product managers really make?

cards.quote: I immediately start sending a regular (weekly) written update on observations, personal areas of focus, and kudos that allows you to scale leadership visibility in an async way.
cards.zh: 我一上任就會開始寄固定的（每週）書面更新，內容分成三塊：觀察、我個人的重點方向、以及 kudos（給人的公開肯定），這樣可以用非同步的方式把領導的能見度放大。
cards.why: kudos 在英語職場是一個標準的欄位名稱——固定在週報裡留一格給別人的功勞。把肯定制度化，它才不會只在你心情好的時候發生。
swaps: Weekly update — observations / focus areas / kudos.
Kudos this week: [人名] for [具體事情].
cards.episode: How to make an impact in your first 90 days

cards.pattern: Special thanks to [群體] who [貢獻]. Your [貢獻] will help us [結果].
cards.quote: Special thanks to the nearly 200 tech professionals who shared their insights again for this follow-up research. Your candid feedback will help us deal with burnout in the tech industry.
cards.zh: 特別感謝將近兩百位再度為這份後續研究分享見解的科技工作者。你們坦率的回饋會幫助我們處理這個產業的職業倦怠問題。
cards.why: 第二句才是重點：Your X will help us Y——告訴對方他付出的東西會變成什麼。少了這句，感謝就只是禮貌；有了這句，對方下次還會再幫你。
swaps: Special thanks to [群體] for [貢獻]. Your input will shape [結果].
Huge thanks to everyone who [動作]—it directly changed [什麼].
cards.episode: How tech’s most resilient workers handle burnout

cards.pattern: Regularly share what you're doing, what you plan to do, and what you've done with [對象].
cards.quote: Regularly share what you're doing, what you plan to do, and what you've done with your manager. It's nearly impossible to over-communicate.
cards.zh: 定期跟你的主管同步你正在做什麼、打算做什麼、已經做完什麼。基本上不可能溝通過頭。
cards.why: 三個時態一次講完（進行中／未來／已完成）是英文週報的骨架，一句就把「我在忙」變成「我可被追蹤」。第二句是給自己的許可：怕囉唆而少寫，是台灣人寫週報最大的失分點。
swaps: Here's what I did last week, what I'm doing this week, and what's coming next.
Sharing my usual three: shipped, in flight, and up next.
cards.pmNote: 週報的價值不是報告，是讓主管在你出事前就有機會介入。
cards.episode: Managing up

cards.pattern: You can also highlight material changes to [X] from the prior [週期] to make it even easier for [對象].
cards.quote: You can also highlight material changes to your priorities from the prior week to make it even easier for your manager
cards.zh: 你也可以特別標出這週跟上週相比有實質變動的優先事項，讓你主管更省力。
cards.why: material changes 是商業書面英文的高頻字，意思是「值得你分心來看的變動」，比 changes 更精準地過濾雜訊。整句把「我幫你篩過了」寫成一個動作。
swaps: Changes since last week are marked in bold.
One material change from last week: [X] moved from P2 to P0.
cards.pmNote: 週報最容易被跳過的原因是每週看起來都一樣；標出差異就有人讀。
cards.episode: Managing up

cards.pattern: Hi [對象], let me tell you about a challenge I ran into ___. Here's how I'm thinking of handling it (or did handle it) ___. Any thoughts?
cards.quote: Hi manager, let me tell you about a challenge I ran into ___. Here’s how I’m thinking of handling it (or did handle it) ___. Any thoughts?
cards.zh: 嗨主管，跟你說一個我碰到的難題 ___。我打算這樣處理（或我已經這樣處理了）___。你有什麼想法嗎？
cards.why: 這個三句模板同時做兩件事：秀出你解決了一個難題，又留一個門讓主管給意見——避免聽起來像邀功，也避免聽起來像卡住了求救。
swaps: Ran into something worth flagging: ___. My plan is ___. Open to a different read.
Quick one: hit ___, handled it by ___. Let me know if you'd have played it differently.
cards.pmNote: 自主性高的人反而更難累積信任，因為主管看不到你做對的決定。
cards.episode: Becoming a senior Product Manager

cards.pattern: As you know, we've generally had a good handle on [X].
cards.quote: As you know, we’ve generally had a good handle on bugs.
cards.zh: 如你所知，我們對 bug 一向控制得還不錯。
cards.why: SCR 架構的 Situation 開場句：先講一句「大家都同意的現況」，讀者才不會在你講壞消息時覺得被突襲。As you know 是禮貌地把共識放上桌，不是在教對方。
swaps: As you know, [X] has been stable for the past few quarters.
Some context first: we've historically had [X] under control.
cards.pmNote: Situation → Complication → Resolution：先講現況、再講變化、最後給答案。
cards.episode: The Minto Pyramid Principle and the SCR Framework

cards.pattern: Recently however, we've seen a large spike in [X], and it's beginning to significantly impact [Y].
cards.quote: Recently however, we’ve seen a large spike in bugs, and it’s beginning to significantly impact our bottom-line.
cards.zh: 但最近我們看到 bug 數量大幅飆升，而且已經開始明顯影響到我們的獲利。
cards.why: SCR 的 Complication 句：however 一個字就把讀者從「還好」切到「有事」。is beginning to 是刻意的——把壞消息定位在「剛開始，還來得及」，而不是「已經完蛋」。
swaps: Over the last three weeks, however, [X] has doubled and it's starting to affect [Y].
That's changed: [X] is now trending in the wrong direction.
cards.pmNote: 壞消息要放在「還能行動」的時間點寫出來，這決定對方是給資源還是給檢討。
cards.episode: The Minto Pyramid Principle and the SCR Framework

cards.pattern: Whenever you're on a call, make sure that anything that's important gets written down: [討論過的選項], [做成的決定], [下一步], plus who is going to do them.
cards.quote: Whenever you’re on a call, make sure that anything that’s important gets written down. Options that were discussed, decisions that were made and next steps, plus who is going to do them.
cards.zh: 只要開了會，重要的東西一定要寫下來：討論過哪些選項、做了哪些決定、下一步是什麼，還有誰負責。
cards.why: 四件事的清單本身就是一份會議紀錄的模板。plus who is going to do them 放在最後不是隨口加的——沒有名字的 next step 等於沒有。
swaps: Notes from today: options considered, what we decided, next steps and owners.
Writing this down so it survives the call: decision, rationale, owner, date.
cards.pmNote: 口頭共識三天後就會有兩個版本；寫下來的那個版本會贏。
cards.episode: This Week #6: Cultivating good relationships with distributed co-workers, building trust to accelerate growth, and leveling up as a PM when you have extra time

cards.pattern: As you are [進行中的工作], get used to sharing updates along the way.
cards.quote: As you are coming up with ideas and thinking through the problem, get used to sharing updates along the way.
cards.zh: 在你還在發想、還在想清楚問題的階段，就要養成一路上不斷同步進度的習慣。
cards.why: along the way 是關鍵——它把「更新」從「有結論才報」改成「過程中就報」。台灣人習慣等做完才講，但共識是在過程中長出來的。
swaps: Sharing where my thinking is at, still early.
Rough notes from the research so far—nothing concluded yet.
cards.pmNote: 在還沒有答案時分享，才有機會讓別人的想法進來變成他們的案子。
cards.episode: Getting buy-in

cards.quote: Stakeholders will feel valued. You’ll stop hearing “I wish you’d looped us in earlier.”
cards.zh: 利害關係人會覺得自己被重視，你也不會再聽到「早知道就早點讓我們知道」這句話。
cards.why: loop someone in 是英文職場最常用的「把某人納入資訊圈」動詞片語，比 inform 溫和且不帶上下關係。這句同時也是你會被抱怨的原句，值得整句記住。
swaps: Looping in [Name] since this touches their area.
Adding [Name] to the thread for visibility.
cards.pmNote: 「太晚才被告知」是跨部門衝突最常見的起火點，而且它跟決定本身無關。
cards.episode: Getting buy-in

cards.quote: Often after a project begins you uncover unexpected hurdles that didn’t inform the estimate.
cards.zh: 專案開始之後，你常常會挖出當初估時程時沒被納入的意外障礙。
cards.why: didn't inform the estimate 把延期的責任放在「當時的資訊」而不是「當時的人」，這是英文報延期最重要的一個轉向——不推責、也不自貶。
swaps: We've hit a few things that weren't visible when we sized this.
The original estimate didn't account for [X].
cards.pmNote: 估時程失準通常不是估錯，是估的時候資訊不足；分清楚這兩者才能改進。
cards.episode: This Week #4: Motivating engineers to hit deadlines, PM career ladders, and aligning with execs

cards.quote: Make it an official change to the date, get buy-in again, and share it widely.
cards.zh: 把它做成一次正式的日期變更，重新取得大家的同意，然後廣泛公告出去。
cards.why: official / again / widely 三個字各擋一種爛作法：偷偷改、自己改、只跟一個人講。這句可以直接當你改期時的行動清單。
swaps: Formally moving the date from [A] to [B]—confirming everyone's still on board.
New target date is [B]. Please flag by [date] if that breaks something on your side.
cards.pmNote: 偷偷延期一次，你之後給的每個日期都會被打折。
cards.episode: This Week #4: Motivating engineers to hit deadlines, PM career ladders, and aligning with execs

cards.quote: “No, but there’s something there. Let’s explore it further. Here’s what I suggest as a next step…”
cards.zh: 不行，但這裡面有東西。我們可以再挖一下。我建議的下一步是……
cards.why: there's something there 是英文裡很漂亮的一句「我沒有否定你」，只用四個字就把對方的面子保住。後面接一個具體 next step，拒絕才不會變成空氣。
swaps: Not as scoped, but the underlying problem is real. Suggest we [X] first.
No for now—but there's a version of this worth testing.
cards.pmNote: 拒絕之後一定要給下一步，不然對方只會再問一次。
cards.episode: Saying no

cards.quote: When asked to make changes to a plan, be transparent about the trade-offs. Don’t assume they know what you know.
cards.zh: 當有人要你改計畫時，把取捨攤開講。不要假設他們知道你知道的事。
cards.why: Don't assume they know what you know 是所有書面溝通的通則，值得當成寫任何一封信之前的檢查句。台灣職場常因為「講了顯得我在抱怨」而省略成本，結果被當成沒成本。
swaps: Flagging the trade-offs in case they're not visible from where you sit.
Sharing the cost side so we're deciding with the same information.
cards.pmNote: 上位者不是不在乎成本，是根本看不到成本。
cards.episode: This Week #0: Advice on growth, product, and leadership

cards.pattern: Identifies issues that will keep [產品] from delivering on time, communicates to leadership, assesses the alternatives to resolve ("path to green"), and builds a plan for resolution.
cards.quote: Identifies issues that will keep the product from delivering on time and/or with the desired requirements and communicates to leadership; assesses the alternatives to resolve (“path to green”) and builds a plan for resolution.
cards.zh: 能提早辨識出會讓產品無法準時、或無法達到要求的問題，向管理層說明，評估各種解法（也就是「回到綠燈的路徑」），並做出解決計畫。
cards.why: path to green 是英文職場報進度的核心術語（紅／黃／綠燈），意思是「怎麼把這件事救回正軌」。報延期時只要附上 path to green，你就從報憂的人變成解題的人。
swaps: Status is yellow. Here's the path back to green.
Flagging risk to the date, along with two options to recover it.
cards.pmNote: 紅黃綠燈的重點不是顏色，是每個非綠燈後面有沒有掛一條回到綠燈的路。
cards.episode: Skills PMs need to build

cards.quote: “This project failed. Let me tell you what happened, what we’ve learned, and what we’re recommending as next steps.”
cards.zh: 這個專案失敗了。我來說明發生了什麼、我們學到什麼、以及我們建議接下來怎麼做。
cards.why: 全套語料裡最值得整句背的一句。四個字認賠（This project failed），接著立刻用三段式接管敘事：事實／學習／建議。認錯的句子越短，後面的建議就越有份量。
swaps: We didn't hit the goal. Here's what happened, what we learned, and what I recommend.
Short version: this didn't work. Longer version below, with a recommendation.
cards.pmNote: 報失敗時，敘事權比事實更重要——先講的人定義這件事怎麼被記得。
cards.episode: This Week #7: Effectively communicating about a failure to execs, managing founder expectations, and hiring a Director of PM

cards.quote: Leaders respect people who are clear-headed, up-front, and take responsibility.
cards.zh: 主管敬重的是頭腦清楚、坦白直接、扛得起責任的人。
cards.why: 三個形容詞剛好對應報壞消息的三個動作：分析清楚、先開口、認下來。注意 take responsibility 跟自責無關——它是動作，不是情緒。
swaps: I own this one.
This was my call, and it didn't work.
cards.pmNote: 扛責任跟自貶是兩件事：前者說「這是我的決定」，後者說「我很沒用」。
cards.episode: This Week #7: Effectively communicating about a failure to execs, managing founder expectations, and hiring a Director of PM

cards.quote: The truth will come out. Don’t try to hide it.
cards.zh: 真相一定會浮出來。不要想蓋。
cards.why: 兩句短句，沒有一個修飾語。書面英文在講最硬的道理時反而最簡單——長句會讓它聽起來像在辯論。
swaps: Better you hear this from me than from the dashboard.
Rather flag this now than have it surface later.
cards.pmNote: 壞消息的傷害是「時間 × 意外程度」，越晚講兩個乘數都越大。
cards.episode: This Week #7: Effectively communicating about a failure to execs, managing founder expectations, and hiring a Director of PM

cards.pattern: Make sure [外部關係人] hear the bad news from you first.
cards.quote: Make sure the external stakeholders hear the bad news from you first.
cards.zh: 務必讓外部的利害關係人是從你這邊第一個聽到壞消息。
cards.why: hear it from you first 是英文職場的固定說法，重點在 first——不是「有講」而是「比別人早」。這一個字就是你的信譽。
swaps: Wanted you to hear this from me before it shows up in the weekly numbers.
Flagging early so you're not surprised in Thursday's review.
cards.pmNote: 壞消息從第三方傳到你老闆耳裡，損失的不是專案，是你之後所有的可信度。
cards.episode: Communicating bad news - Issue 26

cards.quote: The trick to sharing bad news effectively is to imagine being on the other side of the table. What would you want to know if you were in charge?
cards.zh: 報壞消息的訣竅，是想像自己坐在桌子的另一邊。如果換你負責，你會想知道什麼？
cards.why: on the other side of the table 是英文換位思考的固定比喻。這句適合當你寫信前的自問句：不是「怎麼講比較不會被罵」，是「他需要什麼才能做決定」。
swaps: Writing this the way I'd want it if I were in your seat.
Putting myself on your side of the table: here's what you'd need to know.
cards.pmNote: 主管要的是「全部、越快越好、還有下一步」，不是「你的感受」。
cards.episode: Communicating bad news - Issue 26

cards.pattern: When sharing the results for the first time, remind [高層] why they decided to give this a shot in the first place.
cards.quote: When sharing the results for the first time, remind leaders why they decided to give this a shot in the first place.
cards.zh: 第一次報結果的時候，先提醒主管們當初為什麼決定要試這件事。
cards.why: give this a shot / in the first place 都是很自然的口語搭配寫進正式信裡。這一步的作用是把「你的失敗」還原成「我們共同的一個賭注」，而且不用明說。
swaps: Worth remembering why we greenlit this: [原因].
Recapping the original bet before we get to results.
cards.pmNote: 沒有背景就報結果，會讓讀者用今天的資訊去審判當時的決定。
cards.episode: Communicating bad news - Issue 26

cards.pattern: Put together a brief doc that includes [背景], [當初的假設], and [正面的質性回饋]. Only then get into the results.
cards.quote: Put together a brief deck (or doc) that includes the background on the project, including the initial hypothesis, how it came together, and the positive qualitative feedback. Only then get into the results.
cards.zh: 先做一份簡短的簡報或文件，寫清楚專案背景、當初的假設、怎麼形成的、以及正面的質性回饋。這些講完，才進到結果。
cards.why: Only then 是全句的關鍵字——它把順序寫成一條紀律。這不是粉飾，是不讓一個數字獨自代表六個月的工作。
swaps: Context first, numbers second.
Background and hypothesis below; results start on page 3.
cards.pmNote: 先給背景再給數字，是報負面結果的標準順序；反過來會讓討論停在情緒上。
cards.episode: Communicating bad news - Issue 26

cards.quote: What did you learn through this experience? What theories did you disprove? What surprised you and your team most?
cards.zh: 這段經驗你學到什麼？你推翻了哪些原本的假設？最讓你和團隊意外的是什麼？
cards.why: 三個問句可以原封不動當成檢討文件的三個小標。disprove a theory 把失敗重新定義成一次成功的實驗——這是英文商業寫作裡很值錢的重新框架。
swaps: What we disproved: [X].
The biggest surprise: [X]. We'd assumed [Y].
cards.pmNote: 新事業的進度該用「學到多少」衡量，不是用「做出多少」。
cards.episode: This Week #7: Effectively communicating about a failure to execs, managing founder expectations, and hiring a Director of PM

cards.quote: When a project fails, sometimes it’s because the idea was bad, but sometimes it’s because it was executed badly.
cards.zh: 專案失敗的時候，有時候是因為點子不好，有時候是因為執行得不好。
cards.why: 把 idea 和 execution 拆開，是在檢討信裡最重要的一刀。沒拆開，整件事就會被草率歸檔成「這方向不行」，包括那些其實值得再試一次的方向。
swaps: The idea still holds; the execution didn't. Here's what I'd change.
This was an execution miss, not a strategy miss.
cards.pmNote: 自己執行的人最容易誤判成「點子錯了」，因為那樣比較不痛。
cards.episode: This Week #7: Effectively communicating about a failure to execs, managing founder expectations, and hiring a Director of PM

cards.quote: When an execution failure happens, they take ownership, explain what was learned, and rapidly remedy the problem.
cards.zh: 執行出包時，他們會扛起責任、說明學到什麼、並且迅速把問題補起來。
cards.why: 這句出自真實的 PM 職級表，等於把「怎麼報失敗」寫成升遷標準。三個動詞的順序不能換：先扛、再學、再修。
swaps: Owning this: here's what went wrong, what we learned, and the fix already in flight.
My miss. Root cause below, fix ships Thursday.
cards.pmNote: 「扛責任」在職級表裡是資深的定義之一，不是禮貌，是能力。
cards.episode: Skills PMs need to build

cards.quote: Instead of: “Sorry, I messed up” Say: “I’ll fix that now”
cards.zh: 不要說「抱歉，是我搞砸了」，改說「我現在就修好」。
cards.why: 同樣是承認出錯，前者把讀者的注意力留在你的失誤上，後者移到解決上。這對習慣先道歉三行的台灣寫信者是最直接的一刀。
swaps: On it—fix going out this afternoon.
Caught it. Correcting now, will confirm when it's live.
cards.pmNote: 在英文書面溝通裡，不必要的 sorry 會被讀成缺乏掌控感，而不是有禮貌。
cards.episode: Getting buy-in

cards.quote: find a way to make it feel like less of a failure and more of an evolution based on new learnings
cards.zh: 想辦法讓它看起來不像失敗，而像是根據新學到的東西做出的演進。
cards.why: less of a X and more of a Y 是英文重新框架事情最常用的句型，可以直接套進任何一封說明變更的信。evolution 這個字的作用是把轉向寫成連續，而不是斷裂。
swaps: This is less of a pivot and more of a sharpening.
Not a reversal—an update based on what we've learned since.
cards.pmNote: 同一個轉向講成「失敗」還是「演進」，會決定團隊士氣往哪走。
cards.episode: This Week #7: Effectively communicating about a failure to execs, managing founder expectations, and hiring a Director of PM

cards.quote: When you change your point of view based on new information, share it publicly. Make it very clear you aren’t stuck in your views.
cards.zh: 當你因為新資訊改變了看法，公開講出來。讓大家很清楚看到你不是死抱著自己的立場。
cards.why: share it publicly 是重點：改變想法只有被看見才會轉成信譽。stuck in your views 是常見說法，指「被自己的立場卡住」。
swaps: Changing my mind on this—here's what moved me.
I argued for [X] last month. New data says [Y]. Updating.
cards.pmNote: 公開改變想法，是讓別人願意跟你辯論的前提。
cards.episode: 14 habits of highly effective product managers

cards.quote: “Normally, I want you all to feel great about the direction, but I feel strongly about this path, so can we just try it and see how it goes? If I’m wrong, I’m wrong, and I’ll take full responsibility.”
cards.zh: 平常我希望大家對方向都有好感覺，但這條路我立場很堅定，我們就先試試看好嗎？如果我錯了就是我錯了，我會全部扛下來。
cards.why: 先承認自己在破例（Normally...），再堅持，再把風險攬到自己身上。If I'm wrong, I'm wrong 的重複很口語但很有力，讓「我決定了」不變成「我不聽了」。
swaps: I know this isn't consensus. I'm making the call and I'll own the outcome.
Overriding on this one—if it goes badly, that's on me.
cards.pmNote: 團隊多半不介意意見沒被採納，他們介意的是沒被聽見。
cards.episode: Autonomy vs. direction - Issue 35

cards.pattern: I disagree and commit and hope it becomes [最好的結果].
cards.quote: I wrote back right away with “I disagree and commit and hope it becomes the most watched thing we’ve ever made.”
cards.zh: 我馬上回信：「我不同意，但我支持，而且希望它成為我們做過最多人看的東西。」
cards.why: disagree and commit 是矽谷最實用的一句話：一次說完「我保留意見」和「我不會扯後腿」。後半句的祝福讓它不帶怨氣。
swaps: Disagree and commit—count me in on execution.
Still not sold, but I'm behind it. Let's go.
cards.pmNote: disagree and commit 的價值在速度：省下說服你的那幾週。
cards.episode: Autonomy vs. direction - Issue 35

cards.quote: Hear your team out, take their perspectives into account, but make your decision. Then share your thinking behind the decisions.
cards.zh: 把團隊的話聽完、把他們的觀點納入考量，但決定還是你要下。然後把你決定背後的思路講出來。
cards.why: hear someone out 是「讓對方講完」的固定片語（不只是 listen）。最後那句 share your thinking 是關鍵：決定本身不會讓人服氣，理由才會。
swaps: Decision below, plus the reasoning so you can push back on the reasoning.
Here's the call and why—open to being wrong on the why.
cards.pmNote: 決定要快，理由要寫下來；沒寫下來的理由三週後會被重新爭論一次。
cards.episode: Autonomy vs. direction - Issue 35

cards.pattern: Simply communicate to [對象] that you plan to [做法], and ask them to let you know by [日期] if they disagree.
cards.quote: simply communicate to leadership and associated teams that you plan to tackle a project in an ambiguous area, and ask them to let you know by a specific date if they disagree
cards.zh: 就直接告訴管理層跟相關團隊你打算要做這件事，並請他們在某個特定日期前告訴你有沒有反對。
cards.why: by a specific date 把「等批准」翻轉成「反對請出聲」。這是非同步組織裡最重要的一招，重點是它是通知（heads up），不是請示。
swaps: Planning to start on [X] Monday—flag by Friday if you see a problem.
Proceeding unless I hear otherwise by [date].
cards.pmNote: 關鍵是不要卡在等批准；同時要持續回報進度，否則這招會變成先斬後奏。
cards.episode: This Week #9: Breaking into growth, leading with influence, and (not) stepping on toes 🦶

cards.quote: Say no. Or “not yet.” Prioritizing is another word for sequencing—make it clear that if it isn’t a priority today, that doesn’t mean it won’t ever happen.
cards.zh: 說不。或說「還不是時候」。排優先順序其實就是排順序——要講清楚，今天不是優先，不代表永遠不做。
cards.why: not yet 這兩個字讓被砍掉的人不覺得被判死刑。prioritizing = sequencing 這個等式，可以直接寫進說明變更的信裡當一段話。
swaps: Not yet, not never—this sits behind [X] for now.
Deprioritized for this quarter, still on the list.
cards.pmNote: 砍需求時給對方「什麼條件下會被重新考慮」，比給理由更有效。
cards.episode: 14 habits of highly effective product managers

cards.quote: “If X, then A is the best choice. If Y, then B is the best choice. I think this situation is X, so A.”
cards.zh: 如果是 X，A 最好；如果是 Y，B 最好。我判斷這次是 X，所以選 A。
cards.why: 這個句型讓你在展現思考深度的同時仍然給出答案。多數人停在 It depends 就結束了——最後那句 so A 才是資深跟不資深的分界。
swaps: Depends on whether [X] holds. I believe it does, so I'd go with A.
Two worlds here. I think we're in the first one, which points to A.
cards.pmNote: 只講 it depends 是逃避決定；講完條件還要押一邊。
